title.zh: 卷一百九十七 列傳第八十四: 孝友一
title.en: Volume 197 Biographies 84: Filial and Brotherly Acts 1
title.raw: 卷一百九十七 列傳第八十四: 孝友一 Volume 197 Biographies 84: Filial and Brotherly Acts 1

sentences.zh: 世言先王沒，民無善俗。

translations.literal: The world says that when the former kings passed away, the people had no good customs.
translations.idiomatic: It is commonly said that once the ancient kings were gone, the people lost their wholesome customs.

sentences.zh: 元有天下，其教化未必古若也，而民以孝義聞者，蓋不乏焉。

translations.literal: The Yuan possessed the realm; its transformation and instruction were not necessarily like antiquity, yet those among the people renowned for filial piety and righteousness were surely not scarce.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan held the empire, its moral teaching may not have matched that of antiquity, yet men noted for filial devotion and righteous conduct were hardly rare.

sentences.zh: 豈非天理民彝之存於人心者，終不可泯歟！

translations.literal: Is it not that the heavenly principle and the people's constant norms preserved in human hearts can in the end never be extinguished!
translations.idiomatic: Surely what heaven ordains and what binds society together in the human heart can never be wholly effaced!

sentences.zh: 上之人苟能因其所不泯者，復加勸獎而興起之，則三代之治，亦可以漸復矣。

translations.literal: If those above could, relying on what had not been extinguished, again apply exhortation and rewards to raise it up, then the governance of the Three Dynasties could also be gradually restored.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers would build on what still survived in people's hearts, encouraging and rewarding it until it flourished again, the order of the Three Dynasties might gradually be restored as well.

sentences.zh: 今觀史氏之所載，其事親篤孝者，則有臨江劉良臣，汴梁陳善，同官強安，沈州高守質，安豐高澤，鞏昌王欽，修武員思忠，榆縣王士寧，河南朱友諒，泉州葉森，寧陵呂德，汲縣劉淇，建昌鄭佛生，堂邑張復亨，保定邢政，寧夏趙那海，臨潼任居敬，隴西周慶、徐德興，汝寧李從善，華州要敬，色目氏沙的。

translations.literal: Now observing what the historians recorded, those who served their parents with devoted filial piety included Liu Liangchen of Linjiang, Chen Shan of Bianliang, Qiang An of Tongguan, Gao Shouzhi of Shenzhou, Gao Ze of Anfeng, Wang Qin of Gongchang, Yuan Sizhong of Xiuwu, Wang Shining of Yuxian, Zhu Youliang of Henan, Ye Sen of Quanzhou, Lü De of Ningling, Liu Qi of Jixian, Zheng Fosheng of Jianchang, Zhang Fuheng of Tangyi, Xing Zheng of Baoding, Zhao Nahai of Ningxia, Ren Jujing of Lintong, Zhou Qing and Xu Dexing of Longxi, Li Congshan of Runing, Yao Jing of Huazhou, and Shadi of the Semu people.
translations.idiomatic: In the historians' accounts we find, among those famed for deep devotion to their parents, Liu Liangchen of Linjiang, Chen Shan of Bianliang, Qiang An of Tongguan, Gao Shouzhi of Shenzhou, Gao Ze of Anfeng, Wang Qin of Gongchang, Yuan Sizhong of Xiuwu, Wang Shining of Yuxian, Zhu Youliang of Henan, Ye Sen of Quanzhou, Lü De of Ningling, Liu Qi of Jixian, Zheng Fosheng of Jianchang, Zhang Fuheng of Tangyi, Xing Zheng of Baoding, Zhao Nahai of Ningxia, Ren Jujing of Lintong, Zhou Qing and Xu Dexing of Longxi, Li Congshan of Runing, Yao Jing of Huazhou, and Shadi, a Semu.

sentences.zh: 其居喪廬墓者，則有太原王構，萊州任梓，平灤王振，北京張洪範，登封王佐，下蔡許從政、張鐩，富平王賈僧，鄭州段好仁、趙璧、薛明善、張齊，汴梁韓榮、劉斌、張裕、何泰、史恪、高成、鄧孝祖、李文淵、杜天麟、張顯祖，涇陽張國祥，延安王旻，東昌張翬，永平梁訥，高唐鄭榮、劉居敬，同州趙良，南陽周郁、陳介、劉權，大同高著、江鬱、毛翔，歸德葛祥、張德成、張遜、王珪、劉弼，汲縣徐昌祖，真定宋貞、王世賢，晉寧史貴，保定耿德溫、張行一、賈秉實、張勗，河南王宗道、孫裔、夾谷天祐，趙州趙德隆，安豐王德新、石思讓、翼寧、何溥，大都王麟、李簡，華陰李寧、屈秀，懷慶侯榮、丁用、郭天一，耀州王思，中牟閻讓，曹州鄧淵、呂政，徐州胡居仁、張允中，衛輝王慶，福建朱虞龍，隨州高可燾，濟寧魏鐸，武康王子中，淮安翟諟，汶上趙恆，須城許時中，衡山歐陽誠复，江陵穆堅，蘇州王欽，定陶元顯祖，絳州姚好智，宿州孫克忠，集慶傅霖，濟南宋懷忠、牟克孝，汝寧張郁，泉州黃道賢、谷城王福，解州靖與曾，般陽戴貞，兗州王治，沔陽徐勝祖，興中石抹昌齡，峽州秦桂華，蒙古、色目氏納魯丁、赤思馬、改住、阿合馬、拜住、木八剌、玉龍帖木兒、鎖住、唐兀歹、晏只哥、李朵羅歹、塔塔思歹。

sentences.zh: 其累世同居者，則有休寧朱震雷，池州方時發，河南李福，真定杜良，華州王顯政，建寧王貴甫，句容王榮、周成，鄢陵夏全，保定成珪，開平溫義，大同王瑞之，平江湯文英，鄜州員從政，江州范士奇，涇州李子才，宿州王珍。

translations.literal: Those who lived together for successive generations included Zhu Zhenlei of Xiuning, Fang Shifa of Chizhou, Li Fu of Henan, Du Liang of Zhending, Wang Xianzheng of Huazhou, Wang Guifu of Jianning, Wang Rong and Zhou Cheng of Jurong, Xia Quan of Yanling, Cheng Gui of Baoding, Wen Yi of Kaiping, Wang Ruizhi of Datong, Tang Wenying of Pingjiang, Yuan Congzheng of Fuzhou, Fan Shiji of Jiangzhou, Li Zicai of Jingzhou, and Wang Zhen of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Among those whose families dwelt together for generations were Zhu Zhenlei of Xiuning, Fang Shifa of Chizhou, Li Fu of Henan, Du Liang of Zhending, Wang Xianzheng of Huazhou, Wang Guifu of Jianning, Wang Rong and Zhou Cheng of Jurong, Xia Quan of Yanling, Cheng Gui of Baoding, Wen Yi of Kaiping, Wang Ruizhi of Datong, Tang Wenying of Pingjiang, Yuan Congzheng of Fuzhou, Fan Shiji of Jiangzhou, Li Zicai of Jingzhou, and Wang Zhen of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 其散財周急者，則有河南高顏和，台州程遠大，潭州湯居恭、李孔英，建康湯大有，吉州劉如翁、嚴用父，高唐孟恭，松江管仲德、章夢賢、夏椿，江陵陳一寧，中興傅文鼎，永州唐必榮，濟南李恭，寧夏何惠月。

translations.literal: Those who distributed wealth to relieve urgent need included Gao Yanhe of Henan, Cheng Yuanda of Taizhou, Tang Jugong and Li Kongying of Tanzhou, Tang Dayou of Jiankang, Liu Ruweng and Yan Yongfu of Jizhou, Meng Gong of Gaotang, Guan Zhongde, Zhang Mengxian, and Xia Chun of Songjiang, Chen Yining of Jiangling, Fu Wending of Zhongxing, Tang Birong of Yongzhou, Li Gong of Jinan, and He Huiyue of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Those who gave away their property to help others in distress included Gao Yanhe of Henan, Cheng Yuanda of Taizhou, Tang Jugong and Li Kongying of Tanzhou, Tang Dayou of Jiankang, Liu Ruweng and Yan Yongfu of Jizhou, Meng Gong of Gaotang, Guan Zhongde, Zhang Mengxian, and Xia Chun of Songjiang, Chen Yining of Jiangling, Fu Wending of Zhongxing, Tang Birong of Yongzhou, Li Gong of Jinan, and He Huiyue of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 天子皆嘗表其門閭，或復其家。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven on each occasion displayed [honor] at their gates and lanes, or restored their households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had in each case honored their households with inscribed placards at the gate, or exempted their families from service.

sentences.zh: 故援《唐史》之例，具列姓名於篇端。

translations.literal: Therefore, following the precedent of the Tang History, their names are fully listed at the head of the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Following the precedent set by the Tang History, their names are therefore listed in full at the opening of this chapter.

sentences.zh: 擇其事蹟尤彰著者，复別為之傳云。

translations.literal: Those whose deeds were especially striking are again set apart in individual biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose deeds were especially remarkable are given separate biographies below.

sentences.zh: 王閏，東平須城人。

translations.literal: Wang Run, a native of Xucheng in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Run was from Xucheng in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 父素多資，既老，盡廢之，不甘淡薄，每食必需魚肉，閏朝夕勤苦入市，營奉無闕。

translations.literal: His father had long been wealthy; when he grew old he squandered it all, unwilling to live plainly, and at every meal required fish and meat. Run toiled morning and evening in the market so that his father's support never lacked.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been wealthy, but in old age he spent everything and refused a simple life, insisting on fish and meat at every meal. Run worked hard in the market from dawn to dusk so his father wanted for nothing.

sentences.zh: 父性復乖戾，閏左右承順，甚得其歡心，鄉里稱焉。

translations.literal: His father's nature was again perverse and harsh; Run attended him on either side in compliance and won his heart's delight, and the village praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His father was difficult and irascible, yet Run humored him on every side and won his affection; neighbors spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 父嘗臥疾，夜燃長明燈室中，火延籬壁間。

translations.literal: His father once lay ill; at night a long-burning lamp was lit in the room, and fire spread to the fence and wall.
translations.idiomatic: Once when his father was ill, a lamp burned all night in the room until fire caught the fence and wall.

sentences.zh: 閏聞火聲，驚起馳救，火已熾，煙焰蔽寢戶。

translations.literal: Hearing the fire, Run started up in alarm and ran to rescue it; the blaze was already fierce, and smoke and flame veiled the sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Run heard the blaze, leapt up, and rushed to fight it, but the fire was already fierce and smoke and flame hid the bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 閏突入火中，解衣蒙父，抱而出，肌體灼爛，而父無少傷。

translations.literal: Run plunged into the fire, stripped off his clothes to cover his father, and carried him out; his flesh was burned and mangled, yet his father suffered not the slightest harm.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed into the flames, wrapped his father in his own clothes, and carried him out. His body was badly burned, but his father was unhurt.

sentences.zh: 一女不能救，遂焚死。

translations.literal: One daughter could not be saved and was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter whom he could not reach perished in the fire.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，復其役。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, his labor service was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong (1261), his corvée labor was remitted.

sentences.zh: 郭道卿，興化莆田人。

translations.literal: Guo Daoqing, a native of Putian in Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Daoqing was from Putian in Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 四世祖義重至孝，宋紹興間有詔旌之，鄉里為立孝子祠。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Yi was profoundly filial; in the Shaoxing era of the Song an edict honored him, and the village erected a Filial Son Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations back, his ancestor Yi was famed for deep filial piety; in the Shaoxing period of the Song the court commended him and the locality built a Filial Son Shrine.

sentences.zh: 至元初內附。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhiyuan era they submitted to the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhiyuan era (1264) they submitted to the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 閩盜起，居人竄匿，道卿與弟佐卿獨守孝子祠不忍去，遂俱被執。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Min, the inhabitants fled and hid; Daoqing and his younger brother Zuoging alone guarded the Filial Son Shrine and would not leave, and both were seized.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Fujian, neighbors fled, but Daoqing and his brother Zuoging alone stayed to guard the Filial Son Shrine and were both captured.

sentences.zh: 盜將殺佐卿，道卿泣告曰：「吾有兒已長，弟弱子幼，請代弟死。」

translations.literal: The bandits were about to kill Zuoging; Daoqing wept and pleaded, saying, "I already have a grown son; my brother is weak and his children are young—please let me die in my brother's place."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were about to kill Zuoging. Daoqing wept and said, "I have a grown son, but my brother is young and his children are small. Kill me instead of him."

sentences.zh: 佐卿亦泣告曰：「吾家事賴兄以理，請殺我。」

translations.literal: Zuoging also wept and pleaded, saying, "Our household affairs depend on my elder brother to manage them—please kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Zuoging wept as well: "Our family relies on my brother to manage its affairs. Kill me."

sentences.zh: 道卿固引頸請刃。

translations.literal: Daoqing firmly stretched out his neck and begged for the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing stubbornly offered his neck to the sword.

sentences.zh: 盜相顧曰：「汝孝門兄弟若此，吾何忍害。」

translations.literal: The bandits looked at one another and said, "You brothers of a filial household are like this—how can we bear to harm you?"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits looked at one another and said, "Brothers of a house famed for filial piety like this—how could we harm you?"

sentences.zh: 兩釋之。

translations.literal: They released both.
translations.idiomatic: They released them both.

sentences.zh: 道卿年八十，子廷煒為建寧路平準行用庫使，辭歸侍養。

translations.literal: Daoqing was eighty years old; his son Tingwei was director of the Pingzhun treasury at Jianning Circuit and resigned to return home and serve his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoqing was eighty, his son Tingwei, who served as director of the circuit treasury at Jianning, resigned to nurse him at home.

sentences.zh: 道卿嘗病疝，危甚，廷煒憂瘁扶護，一夕發盡白。

translations.literal: Daoqing once suffered from hernia and was gravely ill; Tingwei, worn with grief, supported and tended him, and in one night his hair turned entirely white.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing once fell gravely ill with hernia; Tingwei nursed him in anguish until his hair turned white in a single night.

sentences.zh: 有司言狀，旌之。

translations.literal: The authorities reported the circumstances, and he was honored.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the case and the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 蕭道壽，京兆興平人。

translations.literal: Xiao Daoshou, a native of Xingping in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daoshou was from Xingping in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 家貧，鬻筬以自給。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he sold weaving reeds to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; he sold loom reeds to get by.

sentences.zh: 母年八十餘，道壽事養盡禮。

translations.literal: His mother was over eighty years old; Daoshou served and nourished her with full ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was over eighty, and he cared for her with scrupulous ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 每旦，候母起，夫婦親侍盥櫛。

translations.literal: Each dawn he waited for his mother to rise; husband and wife personally attended her washing and combing.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he waited for her to rise; he and his wife personally helped her wash and comb her hair.

sentences.zh: 日三飯，必待母食，然後退就食。

translations.literal: For the three daily meals he always waited until his mother had eaten before withdrawing to take his own food.
translations.idiomatic: At the three daily meals he would not eat until she had finished.

sentences.zh: 至夕，必待母寢，然後退就寢。

translations.literal: In the evening he always waited until his mother slept before withdrawing to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: At night he would not retire until she had gone to sleep.

sentences.zh: 出外必以告，母許乃敢出。

translations.literal: Whenever he went out he had to inform her, and he dared not leave until his mother consented.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out he told her first and would not leave without her permission.

sentences.zh: 母或怒，欲罰之，道壽自進杖，伏地以受。

translations.literal: When his mother grew angry and wished to punish him, Daoshou would himself bring the staff and lie prostrate to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: If she grew angry and meant to punish him, he brought the rod himself and lay down to receive the blows.

sentences.zh: 杖足，母命起，乃起。

translations.literal: When the beating was finished, his mother ordered him to rise, and only then did he rise.
translations.idiomatic: When she told him to get up, only then did he rise.

sentences.zh: 起復再拜，謝違教，拱立左右，俟色喜乃退。

translations.literal: Having risen he bowed again twice, apologized for having violated her teaching, and stood deferentially at her side until her countenance brightened before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed again, apologized for his fault, and stood at her side until her expression softened.

sentences.zh: 母嘗有疾，醫累歲不能療，道壽刲股肉啖之而愈。

translations.literal: His mother once fell ill; physicians for years could not cure her; Daoshou cut flesh from his thigh for her to eat and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Once when she was ill for years without cure, he cut flesh from his thigh for her to eat and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，賜羊酒，表其門。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, he was granted sheep and wine and his gate was honored with an inscribed placard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan (1271) he received sheep and wine and an honorific placard at his gate.

sentences.zh: 郭狗狗，平陽翼城人。

translations.literal: Guo Gougou, a native of Yicheng in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Gougou was from Yicheng in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 父寧，為欽察先鋒使首領官，戍大良平。

translations.literal: His father Ning served as chief of the Qincha vanguard and was garrisoned at Daliangping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning was a Qincha vanguard officer garrisoned at Daliangping.

sentences.zh: 宋將史太尉來攻，夜陷大良平，寧全家被俘。

translations.literal: The Song general Shi Taiwei came to attack; by night he took Daliangping, and Ning's whole family was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Shi Taiwei attacked, he seized Daliangping by night and took the whole family captive.

sentences.zh: 史將殺寧，狗狗年五歲，告史曰：「勿殺我父，當殺我。」

translations.literal: Shi was about to kill Ning; Gougou, five years old, told Shi, "Do not kill my father—kill me instead."
translations.idiomatic: Shi was about to execute Ning when Gougou, aged five, said, "Do not kill my father. Kill me."

sentences.zh: 史驚問寧曰：「是兒幾歲耶？」

translations.literal: Shi asked in astonishment, "How old is this child?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi asked in amazement, "How old is this boy?"

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「五歲。」

translations.literal: Ning said, "Five years old."
translations.idiomatic: Ning said, "Five."

sentences.zh: 史曰：「五歲兒能為是言，吾當全汝家。」

translations.literal: Shi said, "For a five-year-old child to speak thus, I shall spare your whole household."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "A child of five who can say such a thing—I will spare your whole family."

sentences.zh: 即以騎送寧等往合州。

translations.literal: He then sent Ning and the others to Hezhou by horse.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ning and the others toward Hezhou under escort.

sentences.zh: 道遇國兵，騎驚散，寧傢俱得還。

translations.literal: On the road they met Yuan troops; the horsemen scattered in alarm, and Ning's family all returned home.
translations.idiomatic: They met Yuan forces on the road; the escort scattered in alarm and the family made it home.

sentences.zh: 御史以事聞。

translations.literal: The censor reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The censor reported the affair.

sentences.zh: 命旌之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be honored.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him honored.

sentences.zh: 張閏，延安延長縣人，隸軍籍。

translations.literal: Zhang Run, a native of Yanchang County in Yan'an, registered in the military rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Run of Yanchang County, Yan'an, was on the military register.

sentences.zh: 八世不異爨，家人百餘口，無間言。

translations.literal: For eight generations they did not divide the kitchen; the household numbered more than a hundred mouths, and there was no discord.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations cooked at one hearth; more than a hundred people lived together without quarrel.

sentences.zh: 日使諸女諸婦各聚一室為女功，工畢，斂貯一庫，室無私藏。

translations.literal: Each day he had the daughters and daughters-in-law gather in separate rooms for women's work; when the work was done it was collected and stored in one treasury, and no room held private stores.
translations.idiomatic: Each day the women worked in separate rooms; when finished, everything went into a common storehouse and no room kept private hoards.

sentences.zh: 幼稚啼泣，諸母見者即抱哺。

translations.literal: When infants cried, whichever mother saw them would take them to nurse.
translations.idiomatic: When a baby cried, whichever woman saw it would nurse it.

sentences.zh: 一婦歸寧，留其子，眾婦共乳，不問孰為己兒，兒亦不知孰為己母也。

translations.literal: One daughter-in-law returned to her natal home and left her child behind; all the women nursed it together, not asking which was one's own child, and the child too did not know which was its own mother.
translations.idiomatic: One daughter-in-law visited her parents and left her child behind; all the women nursed it without asking whose it was, and the child did not know its own mother.

sentences.zh: 閏兄顯卒，即以家事付侄聚，聚辭曰：「叔，父行也，叔宜主之。」

translations.literal: Run's elder brother Xian died, and he entrusted household affairs to his nephew Ju; Ju declined, saying, "Uncle, you are my father's generation—uncle ought to take charge."
translations.idiomatic: When Run's elder brother Xian died, he handed the household to his nephew Ju. Ju declined: "You are my father's generation, uncle—you should head the family."

sentences.zh: 閏曰：「侄，宗子也，侄宜主之。」

translations.literal: Run said, "Nephew, you are the heir of the lineage—nephew ought to take charge."
translations.idiomatic: Run said, "You are the heir of the line, nephew—you should head the family."

sentences.zh: 相讓既久，卒以付聚。

translations.literal: After yielding for a long time, in the end it was entrusted to Ju.
translations.idiomatic: They deferred to each other for a long time until Ju finally took charge.

sentences.zh: 縉紳之家，自謂不如。

translations.literal: Gentry families considered themselves inferior to them.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry families admitted they could not match them.

sentences.zh: 至元二十八年，旌表其門。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan, an honorific placard was displayed at their gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan (1291) their gate was honored with an inscribed placard.

sentences.zh: 又有蕪湖芮世通，十世同居；

translations.literal: There were also Rui Shitong of Wuhu, ten generations dwelling together;
translations.idiomatic: There was also Rui Shitong of Wuhu, whose family dwelt together for ten generations;

sentences.zh: 峽州向存義、汴梁丁煦，八世同居。

translations.literal: Xiang Cunyi of Xiazhou and Ding Xu of Bianliang, eight generations dwelling together.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiang Cunyi of Xiazhou and Ding Xu of Bianliang, eight generations dwelling together.

sentences.zh: 州縣請於朝，並加旌美。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties petitioned the court, and all were further honored.
translations.idiomatic: Their prefectures petitioned the court and all received further commendation.

sentences.zh: 田改住，汶上人。

translations.literal: Tian Gaizhu, a native of Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Gaizhu was from Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 父病不能愈，禱於天，去衣臥冰上一月。

translations.literal: His father was ill and could not recover; he prayed to Heaven, removed his clothes, and lay on ice for a month.
translations.idiomatic: His father fell incurably ill; he prayed to Heaven, stripped, and lay on ice for a month.

sentences.zh: 同縣王住兒，母病，臥冰上半月。

translations.literal: Wang Zhu'er of the same county—when his mother was ill he lay on ice for half a month.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhu'er of the same county lay on ice for half a month when his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 寧豬狗，山丹州人。

translations.literal: Ning Zhugou, a native of Shandan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Zhugou was from Shandan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母年七十餘，患風疾，藥餌不效，豬狗割股肉進啖，遂愈。

translations.literal: His mother was over seventy and suffered wind ailment; medicine did not help; Zhugou cut flesh from his thigh for her to eat and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, over seventy, had a paralytic ailment uncured by medicine; he cut thigh flesh for her to eat and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 歲餘復作，不能行，豬狗手滌溷穢，護視甚周，造板輿載母，夫婦共舁，行園田以娛之。

translations.literal: After more than a year it recurred and she could not walk; Zhugou personally washed her filth and tended her with great care, made a plank litter to carry his mother, and husband and wife together bore it, walking the garden fields to amuse her.
translations.idiomatic: A year later she relapsed and could not walk; he washed her waste himself, built a litter, and he and his wife carried her through the garden to cheer her.

sentences.zh: 後卒，居喪有禮，鄉閭稱焉。

translations.literal: Later she died; he observed mourning with propriety, and the village praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he mourned with full propriety and neighbors praised him.

sentences.zh: 潭州萬戶移剌瓊子李家奴，九歲，母病，醫言不可治，李家奴割股肉，煮糜以進，病乃痊。

translations.literal: Li Jianu, son of Yelü Qiongzi the ten-thousand-household chief of Tanzhou, was nine years old; his mother was ill and the physician said she could not be cured; Jianu cut flesh from his thigh, cooked gruel with it for her to eat, and the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianu, nine-year-old son of the Tanzhou commander Yelü Qiongzi, cut thigh flesh and cooked gruel for his mother when doctors despaired; she recovered.

sentences.zh: 撫州路總管管如林、渾州民朱天祥，並以母疾刲割股，旌其家。

translations.literal: Guan Rulin, circuit intendant of Fuzhou, and Zhu Tianxiang, a commoner of Hunzhou, both cut flesh from their thighs because of their mothers' illnesses, and their households were honored.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Rulin, intendant of Fuzhou Circuit, and Zhu Tianxiang, a Hunzhou commoner, likewise cut thigh flesh for ill mothers and their families were commended.

sentences.zh: 畢也速答立，迷里氏，家秦州。

translations.literal: Biye Sudali, a Mili tribesman, his family in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Biye Sudali, a Mili tribesman of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 父喪，廬墓次，晝夜悲號，有飛鳥翔集，墳土踴起。

translations.literal: When his father died he built a hut at the tomb; day and night he wailed in grief; birds flew and gathered, and the grave earth swelled up.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he kept a mourning hut at the tomb, wailing day and night; birds gathered and the grave mound seemed to rise.

sentences.zh: 又有尹夢龍，中興人。

translations.literal: There was also Yin Menglong of Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yin Menglong of Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 母喪，負土為墳，結廬居其側。

translations.literal: When his mother died he carried earth to make a grave and built a hut beside it.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he piled earth for a grave and built a hut beside it.

sentences.zh: 手書《孝經》千餘卷，散鄉人讀之。

translations.literal: He copied the Classic of Filial Piety by hand in more than a thousand volumes and distributed them among the villagers to read.
translations.idiomatic: He hand-copied more than a thousand volumes of the Classic of Filial Piety for neighbors to read.

sentences.zh: 有羣烏集其冢樹。

translations.literal: A flock of crows gathered in the trees on his grave.
translations.idiomatic: A flock of crows gathered in the trees above the grave.

sentences.zh: 樊淵，建康句容人。

translations.literal: Fan Yuan, a native of Jurong in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuan was from Jurong in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 幼失父，事母篤孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father young and served his mother with deep filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father young and served his mother with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，奉母避兵茅山。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he took his mother to Maoshan to escape soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan (1275) he brought his mother to Maoshan to flee troops.

sentences.zh: 兵至，欲殺其母。

translations.literal: When soldiers arrived they meant to kill his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers came they meant to kill his mother.

sentences.zh: 淵抱母號哭，以身代死，兵兩釋之。

translations.literal: Yuan embraced his mother and wailed, offering his body in place of death; the soldiers released them both.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan clung to her and wept, offering his own life; the soldiers spared them both.

sentences.zh: 三十年，江東廉訪使者辟為吏。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the Jiangdong surveillance commissioner recruited him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293) the Jiangdong surveillance commissioner took him on as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 母亡，奔喪，哀感行路。

translations.literal: When his mother died he rushed home for the funeral; his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he hurried home to mourn; travelers on the road were moved by his grief.

sentences.zh: 服闋，奉神主事之，起居飲食，十年如平生。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he kept her spirit tablet and served it; in rising, resting, eating, and drinking, for ten years it was as when she lived.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he kept her spirit tablet and for ten years ate and slept as if she were still alive.

sentences.zh: 台憲交薦，淵不忍去墳墓，終不起。

translations.literal: The censorial offices jointly recommended him, but Yuan could not bear to leave the grave and in the end never took office.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial offices recommended him, but he would not leave the grave and never accepted office.

sentences.zh: 延祐間，汀州寧化人賴祿孫，母病，值蔡五九作亂，負母從邑人避南山。

translations.literal: During the Yanyou era, Lai Lusun of Ninghua in Tingzhou—his mother was ill when Cai Wujiu rebelled; he carried his mother on his back and followed the townspeople to flee to South Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanyou era, Lai Lusun of Ninghua in Tingzhou—when Cai Wujiu rebelled his mother was ill; he carried her on his back to South Mountain with the townspeople.

sentences.zh: 盜至，眾散走，祿孫守母不去。

translations.literal: When bandits came the crowd scattered and fled; Lusun alone stayed and would not leave his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came everyone fled, but Lusun would not leave his mother.

sentences.zh: 盜將刃其母，祿孫以身翼蔽曰：「勿傷吾母，寧殺我。」

translations.literal: The bandits were about to slash his mother; Lusun shielded her with his body and said, "Do not harm my mother—kill me instead."
translations.idiomatic: They were about to strike her; he covered her with his body: "Do not hurt my mother. Kill me."

sentences.zh: 母渴，不得水，祿孫含唾煦之。

translations.literal: His mother was thirsty and could get no water; Lusun moistened her mouth with his own spittle.
translations.idiomatic: She was thirsty and there was no water; he fed her moisture from his own mouth.

sentences.zh: 盜相顧駭嘆，不忍害，反取水與之。

translations.literal: The bandits looked at one another in startled admiration and could not bear to harm them; they even brought water and gave it to them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits marveled and spared them, even bringing water.

sentences.zh: 有掠其妻去者，眾責之曰：「奈何辱孝子婦！」

translations.literal: Some seized his wife and carried her off; the crowd reproached them, saying, "How can you disgrace a filial son's wife!"
translations.idiomatic: Some took his wife away; the others rebuked them: "How dare you dishonor a filial man's wife!"

sentences.zh: 使歸之。

translations.literal: They made her return.
translations.idiomatic: They sent her back.

sentences.zh: 事聞，並賜褒表。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, all were granted commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported the cases, all were commended.

sentences.zh: 劉德泉，汴梁杞縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Dequan, a native of Qi County in Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dequan was from Qi County in Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 早喪母，父榮再娶王氏，生二子居敬、居元，俱幼，德泉甚撫之。

translations.literal: He lost his mother early; his father Rong remarried a Wang woman, who bore two sons, Jujing and Juyuan, both still young; Dequan nurtured them with great care.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died young. His father Rong remarried Lady Wang, who bore two sons, Jujing and Juyuan, still small; Dequan raised them tenderly.

sentences.zh: 及王氏病卒，乃益相友愛。

translations.literal: When Lady Wang died of illness, they became all the more friendly and loving toward one another.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Wang died, the brothers grew even closer.

sentences.zh: 至元末，歲饑，父欲使析居，德泉泣止不能得，乃各受其業以去。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, when famine struck, their father wished to have them divide the household; Dequan wept and tried to stop it but could not, and each accepted his share of the property and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the famine at the end of the Yuan, their father wanted to split the household. Dequan wept and pleaded in vain; each took his share and moved out.

sentences.zh: 久之，父卒，兄弟相約同爨，和好如初。

translations.literal: After a long time their father died; the brothers agreed to cook together again and were harmonious as before.
translations.idiomatic: When their father died, they agreed to live under one roof again and were as close as ever.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，真定朱顯，自至元間其祖父已分財。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi, Zhu Xian of Zhending—from the Zhiyuan era his grandfather had already divided the property.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhizhi (1323), Zhu Xian of Zhending—his grandfather had divided the family property as early as the Zhiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 至顯，念侄彥昉等年幼無恃，謂弟耀曰：「父子兄弟，本同一氣，可異處乎！」

translations.literal: When Xian came of age, thinking his nephews Yanfang and others were young and without support, he said to his younger brother Yao, "Father, sons, and brothers share one breath of life—how can we live apart!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xian grew up, seeing his nephews Yanfang and others young and helpless, he told his brother Yao, "Fathers, sons, and brothers are one body—how can we live apart?"

sentences.zh: 乃會拜祖墓下，取分券焚之，復與同居。

translations.literal: They then gathered to bow at the ancestral grave, took out the division deeds and burned them, and lived together again.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed at the ancestral grave, burned the division deeds, and moved back in together.

sentences.zh: 延祐間，蔚州吳思达兄弟六人，嘗以父命析居。

translations.literal: During the Yanyou era, the six brothers of Wu Sida of Weizhou had once divided the household at their father's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanyou era, Wu Sida of Weizhou and his five brothers had split the household on their father's orders.

sentences.zh: 思达為開平縣主簿，父卒，還家。

translations.literal: Sida was registrar of Kaiping County; when his father died he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Sida served as registrar of Kaiping County; when his father died he went home.

sentences.zh: 治葬畢，會宗族，泣告其母曰：「吾兄弟別處十餘年矣，今多破產，以一母所生，忍使兄弟苦樂不均耶！」

translations.literal: When the burial was finished he gathered the clan and wept, telling his mother, "We brothers have lived apart for more than ten years; now many are ruined—born of one mother, how can we bear to let our brothers' hardship and ease be unequal!"
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he assembled the clan and wept before his mother: "We have lived apart more than ten years and many of us are ruined. Born of one mother, how can we let some suffer while others prosper?"

sentences.zh: 即以家財代償其逋，更復共居。

translations.literal: He then used the family wealth to pay off their debts and they lived together again.
translations.idiomatic: He used family funds to pay their debts and they reunited under one roof.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀甚。

translations.literal: When his mother died his grief in mourning was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned with devastating grief.

sentences.zh: 宅後柳連理，人以為友義所感。

translations.literal: Behind the house willows grew joined as one trunk; people took it as a response to their brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Willows behind the house grew with fused trunks; people said brotherly love had moved heaven.

sentences.zh: 又有朱汝諧，濮州人。

translations.literal: There was also Zhu Ruhe of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhu Ruhe of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 父子明嘗命與兄汝弼別產。

translations.literal: His father Ziming had once ordered him and his elder brother Rubi to hold separate estates.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Ziming had ordered him and his elder brother Rubi to divide property.

sentences.zh: 子明卒，汝弼家盡廢，汝諧泣請共居。

translations.literal: When Ziming died, Rubi's household was utterly ruined; Ruhe wept and asked to live together.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziming died, Rubi was destitute; Ruhe wept and begged to live together.

sentences.zh: 仲父子昭、子玉貧病，汝諧迎至家，奉湯藥甘旨甚謹。

translations.literal: His uncle's sons Zizhao and Ziyu were poor and ill; Ruhe brought them to his home and served them broth and fine food with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle's sons Zizhao and Ziyu were poor and sick; Ruhe took them in and nursed them with devoted care.

sentences.zh: 後卒，喪葬盡禮。

translations.literal: When they later died he buried them with full ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When they died he gave them full funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 鄉人賢之。

translations.literal: The village considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 州縣各以名聞，表其閭。

translations.literal: Each prefecture and county reported their names, and honorific placards were displayed at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties reported their cases and honored their households.

sentences.zh: 郭回，邵武人。

translations.literal: Guo Hui, a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hui was from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 素貧，年六十無妻，奉母寄宿神祠中，營養甚艱。

translations.literal: Always poor, at sixty he had no wife; he supported his mother lodging in a shrine, and providing for her was very hard.
translations.idiomatic: Poor all his life, at sixty he was unmarried; he lodged with his mother in a shrine and barely kept her fed.

sentences.zh: 母年九十八卒，回傭身得錢葬之。

translations.literal: When his mother died at ninety-eight, Hui hired himself out for wages to bury her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died at ninety-eight, he hired himself out to pay for her burial.

sentences.zh: 每旦詣墳哭祭，十四年不輟。

translations.literal: Each dawn he went to the grave to weep and offer sacrifice, and for fourteen years he never stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Every morning for fourteen years he went to weep and sacrifice at her grave.

sentences.zh: 州上狀，命給衣糧贍濟，仍表異之。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported the circumstances; he was ordered given clothing and grain for support, and further singled out for honor.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect reported his case; the court granted clothing and grain and singled him out for commendation.

sentences.zh: 孔全，亳州鹿邑人。

translations.literal: Kong Quan, a native of Luyi in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Quan was from Luyi in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 父成病，刲股肉啖之，愈。

translations.literal: When his father Cheng fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh for him to eat and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Cheng fell ill, he cut thigh flesh for him to eat and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 後卒，居喪盡哀。

translations.literal: When Cheng later died, Quan mourned with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died he mourned with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 廬墓左，負土為墳，日六十肩，風雨有虧，俟霽則補之。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to make the grave—sixty shoulder-loads a day; if wind or rain damaged it, he waited for clear weather and repaired it.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a hut at the tomb and piled earth on the grave—sixty loads a day; after storms he repaired any damage.

sentences.zh: 三年，起墳廣一畝，高三丈餘。

translations.literal: After three years the mound covered an acre and rose more than three zhang.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the mound covered an acre and stood over three zhang high.

sentences.zh: 張子夔，安西人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zikai, a native of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zikai was from Anxi.

sentences.zh: 父喪，每夜半，以背負土，肘膝行地，匍匐至葬所，篩細土為墳。

translations.literal: When his father died, each midnight he carried earth on his back, moving on elbows and knees along the ground, crawling to the burial place and sifting fine earth for the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, each night he carried earth on his back, crawling on elbows and knees to the grave to sift fine soil onto the mound.

sentences.zh: 陳乞兒，歸德夏邑人。

translations.literal: Chen Qi'er, a native of Xiayi in Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qi'er was from Xiayi in Guide.

sentences.zh: 年九歲，母喪，衣毀，親負土為墳，高一丈，廣十六步。

translations.literal: At nine years old, when his mother died he wore mourning garments and personally carried earth for the grave, one zhang high and sixteen paces broad.
translations.idiomatic: At nine, when his mother died, he wore mourning clothes and piled the grave himself—one zhang high and sixteen paces across.

sentences.zh: 人憫其幼，欲助之，則泣拜而辭。

translations.literal: People pitied his youth and wished to help, but he wept, bowed, and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors offered to help, but he wept, bowed, and refused.

sentences.zh: 又有峨眉趙國安、解州張琛、南陽李庭瑞、息州移剌伯顏、南陽怯烈歹，皆居喪有至行，廬墓次，負土為墳。

translations.literal: There were also Guo'an of Emei, Zhang Chen of Jiezhou, Li Tingrui of Nanyang, Yelü Bayan of Xizhou, and Qieliedai of Nanyang—all observed mourning with utmost conduct, dwelt in huts at the tombs, and carried earth for graves.
translations.idiomatic: Also Guo'an of Emei, Zhang Chen of Jiezhou, Li Tingrui of Nanyang, Yelü Bayan of Xizhou, and Qieliedai of Nanyang—all kept mourning huts at the tombs and piled earth on graves with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 並以有司所請，表異之。

translations.literal: All were singled out for honor at the request of the local offices.
translations.idiomatic: Local offices petitioned and all were commended.

sentences.zh: 楊一，懷孟人。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, a native of Huaimeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi was from Huaimeng.

sentences.zh: 至元間，憐其叔清家貧，密以分契詣神祠焚之，與清同居者三十年，無間言。

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan era, pitying his uncle Qing's poverty, he secretly took the division deed to a shrine and burned it, and lived with Qing for thirty years without discord.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiyuan era, pitying his uncle Qing's poverty, he secretly burned the division deed at a shrine and lived with Qing for thirty years without quarrel.

sentences.zh: 張本，東昌茌平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ben, a native of Chiping in Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ben was from Chiping in Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 篤孝，事伯父、叔父皆甚謹。

translations.literal: Deeply filial, he served his paternal and maternal uncles all with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, he cared scrupulously for his uncles.

sentences.zh: 伯父嘗病，本晝夜不去側。

translations.literal: When his paternal uncle once fell ill, Ben day and night would not leave his side.
translations.idiomatic: When an uncle fell ill, Ben never left his side day or night.

sentences.zh: 复載以巾車，步挽詣岱岳禱之。

translations.literal: He also loaded him on a covered cart and, walking, pulled it to Mount Tai to pray.
translations.idiomatic: He placed him in a covered cart and walked, pulling it to Mount Tai to pray for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 張慶，真定人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qing, a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qing was from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 善事繼母。

translations.literal: He served his stepmother well.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his stepmother with devoted care.

sentences.zh: 伯父泰異居河南，慶聞其貧，迎歸養之。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Tai lived separately in Henan; when Qing heard he was poor he welcomed him home to support him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Tai lived in Henan; learning he was poor, Qing brought him home to support him.

sentences.zh: 供膳豐備，過於所生。

translations.literal: The provisions he supplied were abundant, exceeding what he gave his own parents.
translations.idiomatic: He fed him more generously than he fed his own parents.

sentences.zh: 元善，大名人。

translations.literal: Yuan Shan, a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shan was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 父有昆弟五人，因貧流散江淮。

translations.literal: His father had five brothers who, through poverty, scattered to the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: His father had five brothers who, driven by poverty, scattered across the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 久之，遂客死。

translations.literal: After a long time they died as sojourners.
translations.idiomatic: In time they all died far from home.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，善往尋其骸骨，並迎弟侄等一十五喪而歸，改葬祖父母，以諸喪序列祔於塋次。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhida, Shan went to seek their remains and brought back fifteen coffins of younger brothers and nephews, reburied his grandparents, and arranged the other coffins in sequence beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhida (1311) Shan recovered their bones and brought home fifteen coffins of brothers and nephews, reburied his grandparents, and placed the rest in order at the family grave.

sentences.zh: 州縣以聞，並​​旌其家。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county reported it, and all their households were honored.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures reported the case and their families were commended.

sentences.zh: 趙毓，唐州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu, a native of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu was from Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父福遷鄭之管城。

translations.literal: His father Fu moved to Guancheng in Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu moved to Guancheng in Zheng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先，三世同爨。

translations.literal: For three generations beforehand they had cooked at one hearth.
translations.idiomatic: For three prior generations the family had cooked together.

sentences.zh: 毓官福州司獄，滿歸，以母老不復仕。

translations.literal: Yu served as prison inspector at Fuzhou; when his term ended he returned and, because his mother was old, did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as prison inspector at Fuzhou; when his term ended he came home and, his mother being old, never served again.

sentences.zh: 一日，會諸弟，泣申遺訓，願世世無異處，且祝天歃血以盟。

translations.literal: One day he gathered his younger brothers, wept as he conveyed their father's dying instructions, wished that generation after generation they would not live apart, and prayed to Heaven and swore blood to covenant.
translations.idiomatic: One day he gathered his brothers, wept as he passed on their father's charge that they never live apart, and swore an oath before heaven with a blood covenant.

sentences.zh: 自是大小百口，略無間言，同力合作，家道以殷。

translations.literal: From then on more than a hundred mouths, great and small, had hardly a harsh word; they worked together with one strength and the household grew prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter more than a hundred people lived together without discord, working as one until the family prospered.

sentences.zh: 毓長兄瑞早世，嫂劉氏守志，毓率家人事之甚恭。

translations.literal: Yu's eldest brother Rui died early; his sister-in-law Liu maintained her chastity, and Yu led the family in serving her with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest brother Rui died young; sister-in-law Liu remained widowed, and Yu had the family honor her scrupulously.

sentences.zh: 次兄選繼歿，嫂王氏，毓母以其少，許歸改嫁，王氏曰：「婦無再嫁之義，願終事姑。」

translations.literal: Second brother Xuan died in succession; sister-in-law Wang—Yu's mother, because she was young, agreed to let her remarry; Wang said, "A wife has no principle of marrying twice; I wish to serve my mother-in-law to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Second brother Xuan also died; sister-in-law Wang was young and Yu's mother would have let her remarry, but Wang said, "A wife does not marry twice. I will serve my mother-in-law until death."

sentences.zh: 毓妹贅王佑，佑亡，妹念佑母無子，乞歸朱氏養之。

translations.literal: Yu's sister had married into the Wang family as wife to Wang You; when You died the sister, thinking You's mother had no son, asked to return to the Zhu household to support her.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's sister had married Wang You; when You died she asked to return to the Zhao family to care for his mother, who had no son.

sentences.zh: 人謂孝友節義，萃毓一家。

translations.literal: People said filial piety, brotherly love, chastity, and righteousness were all gathered in Yu's household.
translations.idiomatic: People said filial piety, brotherhood, chastity, and righteousness all dwelt in Yu's family.

sentences.zh: 元貞初，旌之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanzhen, they were honored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanzhen era they were commended.

sentences.zh: 胡光遠，太平人。

translations.literal: Hu Guangyuan, a native of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guangyuan was from Taiping.

sentences.zh: 母喪廬墓。

translations.literal: When his mother died he built a mourning hut at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he kept a mourning hut at her grave.

sentences.zh: 一夕，夢母欲食魚，晨起號天，將求魚以祭，見生魚五尾列墓前，俱有囓痕。

translations.literal: One night he dreamed his mother wished to eat fish; at dawn he cried to Heaven and was about to seek fish for sacrifice when he saw five live fish lined before the grave, each with bite marks.
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed his mother wanted fish; at dawn, about to find fish for sacrifice, he found five live fish before the grave, each with bite marks.

sentences.zh: 鄰里驚異，方共聚觀，有獺出草中，浮水去。

translations.literal: Neighbors were startled and gathered to look; an otter came out of the grass and swam away on the water.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors gathered in wonder as an otter emerged from the grass and swam away.

sentences.zh: 眾知是獺所獻。

translations.literal: Everyone knew the otter had presented them.
translations.idiomatic: All knew an otter had brought the fish.

sentences.zh: 以狀聞於官，表其閭。

translations.literal: He reported the circumstances to the authorities, and an honorific placard was displayed at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He reported it to officials and his gate was honored with a placard.

sentences.zh: 至順間，永平龐遵，母病腫，三年不能起。

translations.literal: During the Zhishun era, Pang Zun of Yongping—his mother had a swelling ailment and for three years could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhishun era, Pang Zun of Yongping—his mother had a swelling illness and could not get up for three years.

sentences.zh: 忽思食魚，遵求於市不得。

translations.literal: She suddenly wished to eat fish; Zun sought them at market but could not obtain any.
translations.idiomatic: She suddenly craved fish; Zun could find none in the market.

sentences.zh: 歸途嘆恨，忽有鯉躍入其舟。

translations.literal: Returning he sighed in regret when suddenly a carp leapt into his boat.
translations.idiomatic: On the way home, sighing in frustration, a carp leapt into his boat.

sentences.zh: 作羹以獻，母悅，病瘥。

translations.literal: He made broth and presented it; his mother was pleased and the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: He cooked it for her; she was delighted and recovered.

sentences.zh: 陳韶孫，廣州番禺人。

translations.literal: Chen Shaosun, a native of Panyu in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaosun was from Panyu in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父瀏以罪流肇州。

translations.literal: His father Liu was exiled to Zhaozhou for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu was banished to Zhaozhou for a crime.

sentences.zh: 韶孫年十歲，不忍父遠謫，朝夕號泣願從。

translations.literal: Shaosun was ten years old; unable to bear his father's distant banishment, morning and evening he wept and cried, wishing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could not bear his father's distant exile; day and night he wept to go with him.

sentences.zh: 父不能奪，遂與俱往。

translations.literal: His father could not dissuade him, and so they went together.
translations.idiomatic: His father could not refuse, and they went together.

sentences.zh: 跋涉萬里，不憚勞苦。

translations.literal: They traveled ten thousand li and did not fear hardship.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled ten thousand li without flinching from hardship.

sentences.zh: 道過遼陽，平章塔出見而憫焉，語之曰：「天子寬仁，罰不及嗣。

translations.literal: Passing Liaoyang, Grand Councilor Tachu saw them and took pity, saying to them, "The Son of Heaven is broad and humane; punishment does not reach descendants.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaoyang, Grand Councilor Tachu saw them and said, "The emperor is merciful; punishment does not fall on sons for fathers' crimes.

sentences.zh: 邊地苦寒，非汝所堪。

translations.literal: The borderland is bitterly cold—not what you can endure.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is bitter cold—not fit for a child.

sentences.zh: 吾返汝故鄉，汝願之乎？」

translations.literal: I can send you back to your old home—would you wish it?"
translations.idiomatic: I can send you home—do you wish it?"

sentences.zh: 韶孫曰： 「既不能以身代父，當死生以之，歸非所願也。」

translations.literal: Shaosun said, "Since I cannot take my father's place in death, I must follow him in life and death; returning is not my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Shaosun said, "If I cannot die in my father's place, I will live and die with him. I will not go home."

sentences.zh: 塔出驚異，以錢賞之。

translations.literal: Tachu marveled and gave him money.
translations.idiomatic: Tachu was astonished and gave him money.

sentences.zh: 大德六年，瀏死，韶孫哀慟，見者皆為之泣下。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade, Liu died; Shaosun's grief was so anguished that all who saw him wept.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dade (1302) Liu died; Shaosun's grief moved all who saw him to tears.

sentences.zh: 肇州萬戶府以聞，命遣還鄉里，仍旌異之。

translations.literal: The ten-thousand-household office at Zhaozhou reported it; he was ordered sent back to his home village and further singled out for honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhou authorities reported it; he was sent home and commended.

sentences.zh: 李忠，晉寧人。

translations.literal: Li Zhong, a native of Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhong was from Jinning.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was deeply filial to his mother.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，地大震，郇保山移，所過居民廬舍，皆摧壓傾圮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade a great earthquake struck; Mount Xunbao shifted, and wherever it passed the dwellings of residents were crushed and overturned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dade (1303) a great earthquake moved Mount Xunbao, crushing every dwelling in its path.

sentences.zh: 將近忠家，分為二，行五十餘步復合，忠家獨完。

translations.literal: As it neared Zhong's home it split in two, traveled more than fifty paces, and joined again; Zhong's house alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Approaching Zhong's home it split in two, passed fifty paces, and closed again; only his house stood untouched.

sentences.zh: 吳國寶，雷州人。

translations.literal: Wu Guobao, a native of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guobao was from Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，父喪廬墓。

translations.literal: By nature filial and brotherly, when his father died he built a mourning hut at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Filial by nature, he kept a mourning hut when his father died.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，境內蝗害稼，惟國寶田無損。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade locusts ravaged the crops within the district; only Guobao's fields were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dade locusts destroyed crops throughout the region, but Guobao's fields alone were spared.

sentences.zh: 人皆以為孝感所致云。

translations.literal: People all considered it caused by the response of filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: People attributed it to the power of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 李茂，大名人，徙家揚州。

translations.literal: Li Mao, a native of Daming, moved his household to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mao, from Daming, moved his family to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父興壽臨卒，語茂曰：「吾病且死，爾善事母。」

translations.literal: When his father Xingshou was about to die of illness he told Mao, "I am ill and about to die—you must serve your mother well."
translations.idiomatic: As his father Xingshou lay dying he told Mao, "I am dying. Serve your mother well."

sentences.zh: 茂泣受命，奉母孟氏益謹。

translations.literal: Mao wept and accepted the charge; he served his mother Lady Meng all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Mao wept and promised; he cared for Lady Meng even more devotedly.

sentences.zh: 母嘗病目失明，茂禱於泰安山，三年復明。

translations.literal: His mother once had an eye ailment and went blind; Mao prayed at Mount Tai'an, and in three years her sight returned.
translations.idiomatic: When she went blind Mao prayed at Mount Tai; in three years she could see again.

sentences.zh: 又願母壽，每夕祝天，乞損己年益母。

translations.literal: He also wished his mother long life; each evening he prayed to Heaven, begging to shorten his own years and add to hers.
translations.idiomatic: He also prayed each night to shorten his life and give the years to her.

sentences.zh: 孟氏竟年八十四而歿，居喪哀慟，聞者傷之。

translations.literal: Lady Meng lived to eighty-four and died; Mao mourned with anguished grief, and those who heard of it were saddened.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Meng lived to eighty-four; Mao mourned with crushing grief and all who heard were moved.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，揚州再火，延燒千餘家，火及茂廬，皆風返而滅。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade Yangzhou burned again; the fire spread to more than a thousand households; when it reached Mao's hut the wind turned back and it went out.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dade (1305) fire swept Yangzhou, destroying more than a thousand homes; when flames reached Mao's hut the wind reversed and the fire died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，旌之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court conferred commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Once officials heard of it, the court honored him.

sentences.zh: 羊仁，廬州廬江人。

translations.literal: Yang Ren was a native of Lujiang in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren came from Lujiang, in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 至元初，阿術兵南下，仁家為所掠，父被殺，母及兄弟皆散去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhiyuan era, when Aju's army marched south, Ren's household was plundered by them; his father was killed, and his mother and brothers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhiyuan reign, Aju's troops swept south. Ren's family was seized—his father was killed, and his mother and brothers were driven apart.

sentences.zh: 仁年七歲，賣為汴人李子安家奴，力作二十餘年，子安憐之，縱為良。

translations.literal: Ren was seven years old; he was sold as a bondservant to Li Zian of Bian; he labored strenuously for more than twenty years, and Zian took pity on him and released him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, Ren was sold as a bondservant to Li Zian of Bian. He toiled for over twenty years until Zian, moved by pity, freed him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 仁踪跡得母於潁州蒙古軍塔海家，兄於睢州蒙古軍岳納家，弟於邯鄲連大家，皆為役，尚無恙。

translations.literal: By tracing them, Ren found his mother at the home of Tahai in the Mongol army at Yingzhou, his elder brother at the home of Yuena in the Mongol army at Suizhou, and his younger brother at the home of Lianda at Handan; all were in servitude but still unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Tracking them down, Ren found his mother in the household of Tahai, a Mongol soldier at Yingzhou; his elder brother with Yuena at Suizhou; and his younger brother with Lianda at Handan. All were still enslaved, but alive.

sentences.zh: 乃遍懇親故，貸得鈔百錠，歷詣諸家求贖之。

translations.literal: He then pleaded everywhere among kinsmen and old friends, borrowed a hundred ingots of paper money, and visited each household in turn to ransom them.
translations.idiomatic: He begged help from every relative and old acquaintance, borrowed a hundred ingots of paper money, and went from house to house to buy their freedom.

sentences.zh: 經營百計，更六年，乃得遂。

translations.literal: He tried every expedient; after six more years, he finally succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He schemed and struggled by every means; six years later, he at last succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大小二十餘口，复聚居為良，孝友甚篤，鄉里美之。

translations.literal: More than twenty people, young and old, gathered together again as commoners; their filial piety and fraternal love were very deep, and the countryside praised them.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty kin, young and old, lived together again as free commoners. Their filial devotion and brotherly affection ran deep, and neighbors praised them.

sentences.zh: 大德十二年，旌其家。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dade, his household was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dade (1308), the court commended his household.

sentences.zh: 又有黃覺經，建昌人。

translations.literal: There was also Huang Juejing, a native of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Huang Juejing, from Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 五歲，因亂失母。

translations.literal: At five years old, he lost his mother in the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: At five, he lost his mother in the turmoil of war.

sentences.zh: 稍長，誓天誦佛書，願求母所在。

translations.literal: When he had grown somewhat, he swore before Heaven and recited Buddhist scriptures, wishing to find where his mother was.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, he vowed before Heaven and chanted Buddhist sutras, praying to learn where his mother might be.

sentences.zh: 乃渡江涉淮，行乞而往，衝冒風雨，備歷艱苦，至汝州梁縣春店，得其母以歸。

translations.literal: He crossed the Yangzi and the Huai, going by begging alms; braving wind and rain, he endured every hardship, until at Chundian in Liang County, Ruzhou, he found his mother and returned home with her.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi and the Huai, begging his way forward through wind and rain and every hardship, until at Chundian in Liang County, Ruzhou, he found his mother and brought her home.

sentences.zh: 章卿孫，蜀人，本劉氏。

translations.literal: Zhang Qingsun was a native of Shu; originally of the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qingsun was from Shu; his original surname was Liu.

sentences.zh: 幼為章提刑養子，與母富氏相失三十八年，遍訪於江西諸郡，迎歸養之。

translations.literal: As a child he was adopted by the intendant Zhang; he lost contact with his mother, Lady Fu, for thirty-eight years; he searched throughout the prefectures of Jiangxi and brought her home to support her.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted in childhood by Intendant Zhang, he was parted from his mother Lady Fu for thirty-eight years. He searched every prefecture in Jiangxi, then brought her home to care for her.

sentences.zh: 俞全，杭州人。

translations.literal: Yu Quan was a native of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Quan was from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼被掠賣為劉餻家奴。

translations.literal: As a child he was captured and sold as a bondservant in the household of Liu Gao.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was seized and sold as a bondservant to Liu Gao.

sentences.zh: 後獲為良，自汴步歸杭，尋其母及姊，得之，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Later he obtained commoner status, walked from Bian back to Hang, sought out his mother and elder sister, found them, and became known for serving his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Later freed to commoner status, he walked from Bian back to Hang, found his mother and elder sister, and became known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 李鵬飛，池州人。

translations.literal: Li Pengfei was a native of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pengfei was from Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 生母姚氏，為嫡母不容，改嫁為朱氏妻。

translations.literal: His birth mother, Lady Yao, was not tolerated by his father's principal wife; she remarried and became the wife of a Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother Lady Yao, rejected by his father's principal wife, remarried and became the wife of a man surnamed Zhu.

sentences.zh: 鵬飛幼，不知也。

translations.literal: Pengfei was young and did not know this.
translations.idiomatic: Pengfei was still a child and knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 年十九，思慕哀痛，誓學醫以濟人，願早見母。

translations.literal: At nineteen, longing and grief overwhelmed him; he vowed to study medicine to save others, wishing to see his mother soon.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, grief and longing consumed him. He vowed to study medicine to heal others, hoping thereby to find his mother sooner.

sentences.zh: 行求三歲，至蘄州羅田縣得焉。

translations.literal: He traveled and searched for three years; he found her in Luotian County, Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For three years he traveled in search of her and found her in Luotian County, Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 時朱氏家方疫，鵬飛起之，遂迎還奉養。

translations.literal: The Zhu household was then stricken with plague; Pengfei treated them and recovered them, then brought his mother home to support her.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu household was then ravaged by plague. Pengfei nursed them back to health, then brought his mother home to support her.

sentences.zh: 久之，復歸朱氏，時渡江省覲。

translations.literal: After a long while, she returned to the Zhu household; from time to time he crossed the river to visit her.
translations.idiomatic: In time she returned to the Zhu household, and he crossed the river from time to time to visit her.

sentences.zh: 既卒，歲時攜子孫往祭墓，終其身。

translations.literal: When she died, each year he took his children and grandchildren to offer sacrifices at her grave, and did so to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: After she died, he took his children and grandchildren to her grave each year to make offerings, and never stopped for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 並以有司所請，旌其閭。

translations.literal: All were commended in their neighborhoods at the request of the local officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the request of local officials, all were honored in their neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 趙一德，龍興新建人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yide was a native of Xinjian in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yide came from Xinjian in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，國兵南伐，被俘至燕，為鄭留守家奴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, when the imperial army marched south, he was captured and taken to Yan, where he became a bondservant in the household of the garrison commander Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan (1275), when the imperial army marched south, he was captured and taken to Yan, where he became a bondservant in the household of Garrison Commander Zheng.

sentences.zh: 歷事三世，號忠幹。

translations.literal: He served three generations of masters and was known as loyal and capable.
translations.idiomatic: He served three generations of the family and was known for loyalty and steadfast service.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，一日，拜請於其主鄭阿思蘭及其母澤國太夫人曰：「一德自去父母，得全生依門下者，三十餘年矣，故鄉萬里，未獲歸省，雖思慕刻骨，未嘗敢言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, one day he bowed and petitioned his master Zheng Asilan and his mother, the Lady of Zeguo, saying, "Since I left my parents, Yide has preserved his life under your gate for more than thirty years; my homeland lies ten thousand li away, and I have not been able to return to visit my parents. Though my longing cuts to the bone, I have never dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida (1308), he one day bowed before his master Zheng Asilan and Asilan's mother, the Lady of Zeguo, and said, "Since I was torn from my parents, I have lived under your roof for more than thirty years. My home is ten thousand li away, and I have never been able to go back. My longing has cut me to the bone, yet I never dared ask.

sentences.zh: 今父母已老，脫有不幸，則永為天地間罪人矣。」

translations.literal: Now my parents are old; if some misfortune should befall them, I would forever be a sinner before Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: My parents are old now. If anything should happen to them, I would be a sinner before Heaven and Earth forever."

sentences.zh: 因伏地涕泣，不能起。

translations.literal: He then prostrated himself on the ground, weeping until he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He fell prostrate, weeping, and could not rise.

sentences.zh: 阿思蘭母子皆感動，許之歸，期一歲而返。

translations.literal: Asilan and his mother were both moved; they granted him leave to return, with a term of one year before he was to come back.
translations.idiomatic: Asilan and his mother were deeply moved. They allowed him to go home, on condition that he return within a year.

sentences.zh: 一德至家，父兄已沒，惟母在，年八十餘。

translations.literal: When Yide reached home, his father and elder brothers were already dead; only his mother remained, aged more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yide reached home to find his father and brothers already dead. Only his mother remained, more than eighty years old.

sentences.zh: 一德卜地葬二柩畢，欲少留事母，懼得罪，如期還燕。

translations.literal: Yide chose ground and buried the two coffins; wishing to stay a while longer to serve his mother, yet fearing offense, he returned to Yan on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: After choosing a site and burying the two coffins, he wanted to stay and care for his mother but feared breaking his promise, so he returned to Yan on time.

sentences.zh: 阿思蘭母子歎曰：「彼賤隸，乃能是，吾可不成其孝乎！」

translations.literal: Asilan and his mother sighed and said, "That lowly bondservant could act thus—how can we fail to complete his filial duty!"
translations.idiomatic: Asilan and his mother sighed and said, "A bondservant could be so filial—how can we stand in his way?"

sentences.zh: 即裂券縱為良。

translations.literal: They thereupon tore up the bond and released him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: They tore up his contract and freed him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 一德將辭歸，會阿思蘭以冤被誅，詔簿錄其家。

translations.literal: As Yide was about to take leave and return home, it happened that Asilan was executed on a false charge, and an edict ordered the registration and seizure of his household property.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Yide was preparing to go home, Asilan was executed on a false charge, and an edict ordered his property registered and seized.

sentences.zh: 群奴各亡去，一德獨奮曰：「主家有禍，吾忍同路人耶！」

translations.literal: The bondservants all fled; Yide alone cried out, "Disaster has struck my master's house—how can I abandon them like a passerby!"
translations.idiomatic: The other bondservants fled. Yide alone cried out, "My master's house is in calamity—how can I walk away like a stranger on the road?"

sentences.zh: 即留不去，與張錦童詣中書，訴枉狀，得昭雪，還其所籍。

translations.literal: He stayed and did not leave; together with Zhang Jintong he went to the Central Secretariat and presented a petition of wrongful conviction; the case was cleared, and what had been registered was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed. With Zhang Jintong he went to the Central Secretariat to plead the injustice. The verdict was overturned and the seized property restored.

sentences.zh: 太夫人勞一德曰：「當吏籍吾家時，親戚不相顧，汝獨冒險以白吾枉，疾風勁草，於汝見之。

translations.literal: The Lady of Zeguo praised Yide, saying, "When officials registered our household, kinsmen would not look our way; you alone risked danger to clear our wrong. In you one sees the steadfast grass in a fierce wind.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Zeguo thanked Yide, saying, "When the officials seized our estate, not one relative would help. You alone risked yourself to clear our name. The fierce wind reveals the tough grass.

sentences.zh: 令吾家業既喪而復存者，皆汝力也，吾何以報汝？」

translations.literal: That our family's livelihood, once lost, was restored—all this is your doing. How am I to repay you?"
translations.idiomatic: That our house, once ruined, stands again—that is all your doing. How can I repay you?"

sentences.zh: 因分美田廬遺之。

translations.literal: She then divided out fine fields and dwellings and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: She divided out fine fields and houses and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 一德謝曰：「一德雖鄙人，非有利於是也。

translations.literal: Yide declined, saying, "Though Yide is a humble man, I did not act for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yide refused, saying, "I am a humble man, but I did not act for gain.

sentences.zh: 重哀吾主無罪而受戮，故留以報主。

translations.literal: I deeply mourned that my master was innocent yet was put to death; therefore I stayed to repay my master.
translations.idiomatic: My master was innocent yet was slain. I stayed to repay him.

sentences.zh: 今老母八十餘，得歸侍養，主之賜已厚矣，何以田廬為！」

translations.literal: Now my old mother is more than eighty; I have been able to return and serve her—the master's grace is already great. What need have I of fields and dwellings!"
translations.idiomatic: My old mother is past eighty, and I have been able to go home and care for her. Your kindness is already more than enough. What need have I of land and houses?"

sentences.zh: 遂不受而去。

translations.literal: He then refused to accept them and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He would not accept them and left.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，旌其門。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing, his gate was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing (1312), the court commended his household.

sentences.zh: 王思聰，延安安塞人。

translations.literal: Wang Sicong was a native of Ansai in Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sicong came from Ansai in Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 素力田，農隙則教諸生，得束脩以養親。

translations.literal: He always worked the fields; in the intervals of farming he taught students, using the fees received to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed for a living and, between seasons, taught students, using their tuition to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 母喪，盡哀。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he mourned her to the full extent.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he mourned her with full grief.

sentences.zh: 父繼娶楊氏，事之如所生。

translations.literal: His father remarried a Yang woman; he served her as though she were his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father remarried Lady Yang, and he served her as if she were his own mother.

sentences.zh: 以家多幼稚，侵父食，別築室曰養老堂奉之，朝夕定省，愈久不怠。

translations.literal: Because the household had many small children who encroached on his father's food, he built a separate dwelling called the Hall for Nurturing the Aged and installed his father there; morning and evening he paid his respects, and the longer it went on, the less he slackened.
translations.idiomatic: With many young children in the house eating into his father's share, he built a separate hall called the Hall for Nurturing the Aged and moved his father there. Morning and evening he attended him, never slackening as the years passed.

sentences.zh: 父嘗病劇，思聰憂甚，拜祈於天，額膝皆成瘡，得神泉飲之，愈。

translations.literal: His father once fell gravely ill; Sicong was deeply worried and prayed to Heaven; his forehead and knees both formed sores from bowing, and he obtained divine spring water to drink, and recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Sicong prayed to Heaven in anguish until his forehead and knees were raw from bowing. He found sacred spring water; his father drank it and recovered.

sentences.zh: 後復失明，思聰舐之，即能視。

translations.literal: Later his father again lost his sight; Sicong licked his eyes, and he was able to see.
translations.idiomatic: Later his father went blind again. Sicong licked his eyes, and sight returned.

sentences.zh: 縣上狀，命表異之。

translations.literal: The county submitted a report, and an order was issued to mark him out for special praise.
translations.idiomatic: The county reported his case, and the court singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 徹徹，捏古思氏。

translations.literal: Cheche was of the Nigusi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheche belonged to the Nigusi clan.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，事母篤孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father in childhood and served his mother with deep filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father died when he was young, and he served his mother with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 稍壯，母歿，慟哭頓絕，水漿不入口者三日。

translations.literal: When he had grown somewhat, his mother died; he wailed until he collapsed, and for three days he took neither water nor food.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, his mother died. He wailed until he collapsed and took no food or drink for three days.

sentences.zh: 既葬，居喪有禮，每節序祭祀，哭泣常如袒括時。

translations.literal: After the burial, he observed mourning with propriety; at each seasonal sacrifice he wept as at the first day of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he observed mourning rites properly. At every seasonal sacrifice he wept as if it were the day she died.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，思慕猶如孩童。

translations.literal: Past forty years of age, his longing was still like that of a child.
translations.idiomatic: Even past forty, he yearned for her like a child.

sentences.zh: 每見人父母，則嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw others' parents, he would sob and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw someone else's parents, he would choke back sobs and weep.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，曰：「人皆有父母，我獨無，是以泣耳。」

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, he said, "All people have parents; I alone have none—therefore I weep."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Everyone has parents. I alone do not—that is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 至大三年，褒異。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida, he was marked out for special praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhida (1310), the court honored him with special praise.

sentences.zh: 王初應，漳州長泰人。

translations.literal: Wang Chuying was a native of Changtai in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuying was from Changtai in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至大四年二月，從父義士樵劉嶺山，有虎出叢棘中，搏義士，傷右肩，初應赴救，抽鐮刀刺虎鼻殺之，義士得生。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Zhida, he followed his father, the righteous man, to gather firewood on Liuling Mountain; a tiger emerged from the thicket, seized the righteous man, and wounded his right shoulder; Chuying rushed to the rescue, drew a sickle, stabbed the tiger in the nose and killed it, and the righteous man survived.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year of Zhida (1311), he went with his father to gather firewood on Liuling Mountain. A tiger burst from the brush, seized his father, and tore his right shoulder. Chuying ran to save him, stabbed the tiger in the nose with a sickle, killed it, and his father lived.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，同縣施合德，父真祐嘗出耘，為虎扼於田，合德與從弟發仔持斧前殺虎，父得生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiding, Shi Hede of the same county—his father Zhenyou had gone out to weed the fields and was seized by a tiger in the field; Hede and his younger cousin Fazi took axes and went forward and killed the tiger, and the father survived.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiding (1325), Shi Hede of the same county—his father Zhenyou was working in the fields when a tiger seized him. Hede and his cousin Fazi took axes, rushed forward, killed the tiger, and saved their father.

sentences.zh: 並旌其門。

translations.literal: Both had their gates commended.
translations.idiomatic: Both households were honored at their gates.

sentences.zh: 鄭文嗣，婺州浦江人。

translations.literal: Zheng Wensi was a native of Pujiang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Wensi came from Pujiang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其家十世同居，凡二百四十餘年，一錢尺帛無敢私。

translations.literal: His family lived together for ten generations, altogether more than two hundred forty years; not a single coin or foot of cloth was kept privately.
translations.idiomatic: Ten generations of his family lived under one roof for more than two hundred forty years. Not a coin or a foot of cloth was kept for private use.

sentences.zh: 至大間表其門。

translations.literal: During the Zhida era, their gate was marked out for praise.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhida era, their gate was singled out for praise.

sentences.zh: 文嗣歿，從弟大和繼主家事，益嚴而有恩，家庭中凜如公府，子弟稍有過，頒白者猶鞭之。

translations.literal: When Wensi died, his younger cousin Dahe succeeded as head of the household; he was all the stricter yet all the more gracious; within the family it was as stern as a public office—if a younger member committed even a slight fault, even those with gray hair were still whipped.
translations.idiomatic: After Wensi died, his cousin Dahe took charge of the household. He was strict yet kind; the home ran like a magistrate's hall. Even a gray-haired member of the younger generation could be whipped for a small fault.

sentences.zh: 每遇歲時，大和坐堂上，群從子皆盛衣冠，雁行立左序下，以次進。

translations.literal: Whenever the seasons came round, Dahe would sit in the hall; the assembled younger cousins all dressed in full ceremonial garb and stood in goose formation on the left in order of rank, advancing one by one.
translations.idiomatic: At each seasonal festival Dahe sat in the hall while the younger cousins, dressed in full ceremonial robes, lined up in ranks on the left and came forward in turn.

sentences.zh: 拜跪奉觴上壽畢，皆肅容拱手，自右趨出，足武相銜，無敢參差者。

translations.literal: After bowing, kneeling, and presenting the cup to offer longevity, all withdrew with solemn countenance, hands folded, hastening out to the right; their steps matched in martial cadence, and none dared fall out of order.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed, knelt, and offered the longevity cup; then, solemn and hands folded, they filed out to the right in perfect step, none daring to break rank.

sentences.zh: 見者嗟慕，謂有三代遺風。

translations.literal: Those who saw it sighed in admiration, saying it had the lingering air of the Three Dynasties.
