translations.idiomatic: Onlookers sighed in admiration, saying the household still breathed the air of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 狀聞，復其家。

translations.literal: When a report reached the authorities, the household was again exempted from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: When officials learned of it, the household was again exempted from corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 部使者餘闕為書「東浙第一家」以褒之。

translations.literal: Yu Que, the circuit intendant, wrote "The First Family of Eastern Zhe" to praise them.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Intendant Yu Que wrote "The First Family of Eastern Zhe" in their praise.

sentences.zh: 大和方正，不奉浮屠、老子教，冠昏喪葬，必稽朱熹《家禮》而行執。

translations.literal: Dahe was upright; he did not follow Buddhist or Daoist teachings; for capping, marriage, mourning, and burial he always consulted Zhu Xi's Family Rituals and carried them out.
translations.idiomatic: Dahe was upright and did not follow Buddhist or Daoist rites. For capping, marriage, mourning, and burial he always followed Zhu Xi's Family Rituals.

sentences.zh: 親喪，哀甚，三年不御酒肉，子孫從化，皆孝謹。

translations.literal: When his parents died, his grief was extreme; for three years he did not touch wine or meat, and his children and grandchildren followed his example, all filial and careful.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he grieved deeply and abstained from wine and meat for three years. His descendants followed his example and were all dutiful and careful.

sentences.zh: 雖嘗仕宦，不敢一毫有違家法。

translations.literal: Though he once served in office, he did not dare violate the family rules in the slightest.
translations.idiomatic: Though he once held office, he never broke the family rules, not even in the smallest matter.

sentences.zh: 諸婦唯事女工，不使預家政。

translations.literal: The women of the clan attended only to women's work and were not allowed to meddle in household governance.
translations.idiomatic: The women did only women's work and were not allowed to manage household affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗族里閭，皆懷之以恩。

translations.literal: Clansmen and neighbors all cherished them for their kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and neighbors all held them in affection for their kindness.

sentences.zh: 家畜兩馬，一出，則一為之不食，人以為孝義所感。

translations.literal: The family kept two horses; when one went out, the other would not eat—people took this as a response moved by filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The family kept two horses; when one went out, the other would refuse to eat. People saw this as a sign stirred by their filial righteousness.

sentences.zh: 有《家範》三卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: There is a Household Standards in three scrolls, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a three-scroll Household Standards that has been handed down through the ages.

sentences.zh: 王薦，福寧人。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a native of Funing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was from Funing.

sentences.zh: 性孝而好義。

translations.literal: By nature he was filial and fond of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and devoted to righteousness.

sentences.zh: 父嘗疾甚，薦夜禱於天，願減己年益父壽。

translations.literal: His father once fell gravely ill; Jian prayed to Heaven at night, wishing to shorten his own years to extend his father's life.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Jian prayed at night to Heaven, offering to shorten his own life in exchange for his father's.

sentences.zh: 父絕而復蘇，告其友曰：「適有神人，黃衣紅帕首，恍惚語我曰：'汝子孝，上帝命錫汝十二齡。'」

translations.literal: His father stopped breathing and then revived; he told his friend, "Just now a divine man in yellow robes with a red turban vaguely spoke to me, saying, 'Your son is filial; the Supreme Lord commands that you be granted twelve more years of life.'"
translations.idiomatic: His father stopped breathing, then revived and told a friend, "A divine man in yellow robes and a red turban just spoke to me: 'Your son is filial. Heaven grants you twelve more years.'"

sentences.zh: 疾遂愈，後果十二年而卒。

translations.literal: The illness thereupon healed; afterward he indeed died twelve years later.
translations.idiomatic: The illness cleared, and twelve years later he died, just as foretold.

sentences.zh: 母沈氏病渴，語薦曰：「得瓜以啖我，渴可止。」

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Shen, was sick with thirst; she said to Jian, "If I could have a melon to eat, the thirst would stop."
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Shen was sick with raging thirst and said to Jian, "If I could eat a melon, this thirst would stop."

sentences.zh: 時冬月，求於鄉不得，行至深奧嶺，值大雪，薦避雪樹下，思母病，仰天而哭。

translations.literal: It was then the winter months; he sought in the village but could not find one; he walked to Shen'ao Ridge; encountering heavy snow, Jian took shelter under a tree and, thinking of his mother's illness, looked up to Heaven and wept.
translations.idiomatic: It was deep winter, and none could be found in the village. He walked to Shen'ao Ridge. Snow fell heavily; he sheltered under a tree, thought of his mother's illness, and wept to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 忽見岩石間青蔓離披，有二瓜焉，因摘歸奉母。

translations.literal: Suddenly he saw green vines spreading among the rocks, with two melons; he picked them and returned to present them to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he saw green vines trailing over the rocks—with two melons on them. He picked them and brought them home to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母食之，渴頓止。

translations.literal: His mother ate them, and the thirst immediately ceased.
translations.idiomatic: She ate them, and her thirst vanished at once.

sentences.zh: 兄孟韐早世，嫂林氏更適劉仲山。

translations.literal: His elder brother Mengge died young; his sister-in-law, Lady Lin, remarried Liu Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Mengge died young. His sister-in-law Lady Lin remarried Liu Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 仲山嘗以田鬻於薦，及死，不能葬，且無子，族以其貧，莫肯為之後。

translations.literal: Zhongshan once sold fields to Jian; when he died, he could not be buried and had no son; the clan, seeing their poverty, would none of them serve as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan had once sold fields to Jian. When he died, there was no money for burial and no son. The clan, seeing how poor they were, would not take him as heir.

sentences.zh: 薦即以田還之，使置後，且治葬焉。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon returned the fields to them, had an heir appointed, and also arranged the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Jian returned the fields, had an heir appointed for the line, and paid for the burial.

sentences.zh: 州禁民死不葬者，時民貧未葬者眾，畏令，悉焚柩，棄骨野中。

translations.literal: The prefecture forbade people to leave the dead unburied; at that time many of the people were too poor to bury their dead; fearing the order, they all burned the coffins and cast the bones out in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture forbade leaving the dead unburied. Many were too poor to comply; fearing punishment, they burned coffins and cast bones into the wild.

sentences.zh: 薦哀之，以地為義阡收瘞之。

translations.literal: Jian mourned this; he set aside land as a charity burial ground and gathered and interred them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian grieved at this. He set aside land as a charity burial ground and gathered the remains for burial.

sentences.zh: 有死不能斂者，复買棺以贈，人皆感焉。

translations.literal: For those who died without means of encoffinement, he again bought coffins and gave them away; all were moved.
translations.idiomatic: For those who died without coffins, he bought coffins and gave them away. All were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，其鄉旱，民艱糴，薦盡出儲粟賑之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhida, his district suffered drought; the people had difficulty buying grain; Jian gave out all his stored grain to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhida (1311), drought struck his district. Grain was scarce; Jian opened his stores and gave everything away.

sentences.zh: 有施福等十一家，飢欲死，薦聞，惻然欲濟之，家粟已竭，即以己田易谷百石分給之。

translations.literal: Eleven households, including Shi Fu, were starving and near death; when Jian heard of it, he was moved with compassion and wished to aid them, but the household grain was already exhausted; he therefore exchanged his own fields for a hundred shi of grain and divided it among them.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven households, including Shi Fu, were starving to death. Jian wanted to help, but his grain was gone. He sold his own fields for a hundred shi of grain and divided it among them.

sentences.zh: 福等德其活己，每月朔，會佛祠為祈福。

translations.literal: Fu and the others were grateful that he had saved their lives; on the first day of each month they gathered at a Buddhist shrine to pray for blessings on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful that he had saved their lives, Fu and the others met at a Buddhist shrine on the first of each month to pray for his blessing.

sentences.zh: 福建宣慰司上狀旌之。

translations.literal: The Fujian Pacification Commission submitted a report and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian Pacification Commission reported his deeds and the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 郭全，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Quan was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan was from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，哀戚如成人。

translations.literal: He lost his mother in childhood and grieved as an adult would.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother as a child and mourned with the grief of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 及壯，父庭玉又卒，居廬三載，啜粥面墨。

translations.literal: When he reached maturity, his father Tingyu also died; he lived in a mourning hut for three years, eating thin gruel until his face turned dark.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, his father Tingyu also died. He lived in a mourning hut for three years, eating thin gruel until his face turned ashen.

sentences.zh: 事繼母唐古氏甚孝。

translations.literal: He served his stepmother, Lady Tanggu, with great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his stepmother Lady Tanggu with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 唐古氏生四子，皆幼，全躬耕以養。

translations.literal: Lady Tanggu bore four sons, all still young; Quan personally farmed to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tanggu had borne four sons, all still young. Quan farmed with his own hands to support them.

sentences.zh: 既長娶婦，各求分財異居，全不能止，凡田廬器物，悉自取朽弊者，奉唐古氏以居，甘旨無乏。

translations.literal: When they had grown and taken wives, each sought a share of the property and a separate household; Quan could not stop them; for fields, dwellings, and utensils he always took for himself the worn and broken ones, installed Lady Tanggu to live on what remained, and never lacked fine food for her.
translations.idiomatic: When they grew up and married, each wanted his share and a separate home. Quan could not stop them. He took the worn fields, houses, and goods for himself, kept Lady Tanggu comfortably housed, and never let her want for good food.

sentences.zh: 唐古氏卒，全年六十餘，哀痛毀瘠，廬其墓終喪。

translations.literal: When Lady Tanggu died, Quan was more than sixty; his grief was extreme and he wasted away; he lived in a hut at her grave until mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Tanggu died, Quan was past sixty. He grieved until he wasted away and kept a mourning hut at her grave until the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 又有劉德，奉元人。

translations.literal: There was also Liu De, a native of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Liu De, from Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 父娶後妻何氏，德事之如所生。

translations.literal: His father remarried a He woman; De served her as though she were his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father remarried Lady He, and De served her as if she were his own mother.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭工取直，寸錢尺帛皆上之。

translations.literal: The household was poor; he hired himself out for wages, and every coin and foot of cloth he turned over to the family.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor. He hired himself out and turned over every coin and every foot of cloth he earned.

sentences.zh: 四弟並何出，德撫愛尤篤。

translations.literal: Four younger brothers were all born to Lady He; De cherished and loved them with especial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He bore four younger brothers, and De loved and cared for them with special devotion.

sentences.zh: 年五十未娶，稱貸得錢先為弟求婦，諸弟亦化其德，一門藹然。

translations.literal: Past fifty he had not yet married; he borrowed money and first found wives for his brothers; the brothers too were transformed by his virtue, and the whole household was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Past fifty, he had not married. He borrowed money and found wives for his brothers first. They in turn were moved by his example, and the whole household lived in harmony.

sentences.zh: 鄉里稱為劉佛子。

translations.literal: The neighborhood called him the Buddha Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors called him the Buddha Liu.

sentences.zh: 馬押忽，也里可溫氏。

translations.literal: Ma Yahu was of the Yelikewen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yahu belonged to the Yelikewen (Nestorian) clan.

sentences.zh: 素貧，事繼母張氏、庶母呂氏，克盡子職。

translations.literal: Always poor, he served his stepmother Lady Zhang and concubine mother Lady Lü, fully fulfilling a son's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Though always poor, he served his stepmother Lady Zhang and concubine mother Lady Lü and fully discharged every duty of a son.

sentences.zh: 劉居敬，大都人。

translations.literal: Liu Jujing was a native of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jujing was from Dadu.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，繼母郝氏病，居敬憂之，懇天以求代。

translations.literal: At ten years of age, his stepmother Lady Hao fell ill; Jujing was worried and pleaded to Heaven, asking to take her place.
translations.idiomatic: At ten, his stepmother Lady Hao fell ill. Jujing was distraught and prayed to Heaven to suffer in her stead.

sentences.zh: 狀聞，並褒表之。

translations.literal: When reports reached the authorities, all were marked out for special praise.
translations.idiomatic: When their cases were reported, all were singled out for special praise.

sentences.zh: 楊皞，扶風人。

translations.literal: Yang Hao was a native of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父清，母牛氏。

translations.literal: His father was Qing; his mother was Lady Niu.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Qing; his mother was Lady Niu.

sentences.zh: 牛氏嘗病劇，皞叩天求代，遂痊，如是者再。

translations.literal: Lady Niu once fell gravely ill; Hao knocked his head to Heaven asking to take her place, and she recovered—this happened twice.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Niu once fell gravely ill. Hao kowtowed to Heaven, offering to die in her place, and she recovered—twice this happened.

sentences.zh: 後牛氏失明，皞登太白山取神泉洗之，復如故。

translations.literal: Later Lady Niu lost her sight; Hao climbed Mount Taibai, fetched sacred spring water, and washed her eyes, and she was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Niu went blind. Hao climbed Mount Taibai, brought back sacred spring water, washed her eyes, and her sight returned.

sentences.zh: 牛氏歿，哀毀特甚。

translations.literal: When Lady Niu died, his grief and emaciation were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Niu died, his grief wasted him away.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，大雨，獨皞墓前後數里，密雲蔽之，雨不沾土，送者大悅。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, heavy rain fell; only for several li before and after Hao's mother's grave did dense clouds cover the sky—the rain did not touch the earth, and those who attended the funeral were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day, rain poured down. Yet for several li around her grave dense clouds shielded the ground, and the rain never touched the soil. Those at the funeral rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，令妻衛氏家居養清，皞獨廬墓上，負土為墳，蔬食水飲，終其喪。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete, he had his wife Lady Wei remain at home to support Qing; Hao alone lived in a hut on the grave mound, carried earth to build the tomb, ate vegetables and drank water, and did so to the end of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he sent his wife Lady Wei home to care for Qing. He alone lived on the mound, heaped earth for the tomb, ate vegetables and drank water, and mourned until the period ended.

sentences.zh: 清卒，亦如之。

translations.literal: When Qing died, he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing died, he did the same again.

sentences.zh: 丁文忠，許州偃城人，業鼓冶。

translations.literal: Ding Wenzhong was a native of Yancheng in Xuzhou and worked as a smith.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wenzhong was from Yancheng in Xuzhou and worked as a metalworker.

sentences.zh: 母和氏疾，與弟文孝竭力調侍。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady He fell ill, he and his younger brother Wenxiao exerted themselves to the utmost in tending and serving her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady He fell ill, he and his younger brother Wenxiao nursed her with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 母卒，文忠廬墓側，不與妻面者三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Wenzhong lived beside the grave; for three years he did not face his wife.
translations.idiomatic: After she died, Wenzhong lived beside the grave and did not look his wife in the face for three years.

sentences.zh: 父貴又疾，醫不能療，文忠造車一輛，兄弟共御之，載父禱於嵩山、五台、泰安、河瀆諸祠，途遇異僧遺藥而愈。

translations.literal: His father Gui again fell ill; physicians could not cure him; Wenzhong built a cart, and the brothers together drove it, carrying their father to pray at the shrines of Mount Song, Mount Wutai, Mount Tai, and the River God; on the road they met a strange monk who gave them medicine, and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui fell ill again, and doctors could not cure him. Wenzhong built a cart; the brothers drove it together, carrying their father to pray at Mount Song, Mount Wutai, Mount Tai, and the River God shrine. On the road a strange monk gave them medicine, and Gui recovered.

sentences.zh: 延祐七年，旌之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanyou, he was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yanyou (1320), the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 邵敬祖，宛丘人。

translations.literal: Shao Jingzu was a native of Wanqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jingzu was from Wanqiu.

sentences.zh: 父喪廬墓。

translations.literal: When his father died, he lived in a mourning hut at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he kept a mourning hut at the grave.

sentences.zh: 母繼歿，河決，不克葬，殯於城西。

translations.literal: His mother died next; the Yellow River broke its banks, and burial was impossible; the coffin was temporarily housed west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died afterward. The Yellow River broke its banks and burial was impossible, so the coffin was kept west of the city.

sentences.zh: 敬祖露宿依其側，風雨不去。

translations.literal: Jingzu slept in the open beside it; through wind and rain he did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu slept in the open beside it and would not leave, rain or shine.

sentences.zh: 友人哀之，為縛草舍庇之，前後居廬六年，兩髀俱成濕疾。

translations.literal: A friend, pitying him, bound together a grass hut to shelter him; for six years before and after he lived in mourning huts, and both thighs developed damp sores.
translations.idiomatic: A friend, pitying him, built a grass shelter. For six years he lived in mourning huts, and sores from damp spread across both thighs.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，旌其家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi, his household was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhizhi (1323), his household was commended.

sentences.zh: 其後又有永平李彥忠，父喪廬墓，八年不至家。

translations.literal: Afterward there was also Li Yanzong of Yongping, who lived in a mourning hut when his father died and for eight years did not go home.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Li Yanzong of Yongping, who mourned his father in a hut at the grave and did not go home for eight years.

sentences.zh: 茶陵譚景星，幼失父，追念之，廬其墓十年。

translations.literal: Tan Jingxing of Chaling lost his father in childhood; remembering him, he lived in a hut at the grave for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jingxing of Chaling lost his father as a child. Longing for him, he kept a mourning hut at the grave for ten years.

sentences.zh: 亳州郭成，年七十一，母喪，食粥廬墓一年，朝夕哭臨。

translations.literal: Guo Cheng of Bozhou, at seventy-one years of age, when his mother died ate only gruel and lived in a hut at the grave for one year, weeping morning and evening at the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Cheng of Bozhou was seventy-one when his mother died. He ate only gruel, lived in a hut at her grave for a year, and wept over the coffin morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 人哀其老而能孝。

translations.literal: People pitied his age yet admired his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: People marveled that at his age he could still be so filial.

sentences.zh: 扈鐸，汴梁蘭陽人。

translations.literal: Hu Duo was a native of Lanyang in Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Duo was from Lanyang in Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 蚤孤，育於伯父。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and was raised by his father's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: His father died young, and he was raised by his father's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 及壯，事伯父如所生。

translations.literal: When he reached maturity, he served his uncle as though he were his birth father.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he served his uncle as if he were his own father.

sentences.zh: 伯父老無子，鐸為買妾，歲餘，產一女。

translations.literal: His uncle was old and had no son; Duo bought him a concubine, and after more than a year she bore a girl.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle was old and childless. Duo bought him a concubine; after a year she bore a girl.

sentences.zh: 其妾性頗不慧，熟寐，壓女死。

translations.literal: The concubine's nature was rather dull; in deep sleep she crushed the girl to death.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine was slow-witted. She slept heavily and smothered the infant girl.

sentences.zh: 久之，伯父卒，鐸喪之甚哀。

translations.literal: After a long while his uncle died; Duo mourned him with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: In time his uncle died, and Duo mourned him with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 遺腹生一男，鐸懲前失，告其母及妻妹護視之，己复廬戶外，中夜審察，不敢安寢。

translations.literal: A posthumous son was born—a boy; Duo, mindful of the earlier loss, told his mother and his wife's sister to watch over him; he himself again lived in a hut outside the door; in the middle of the night he kept watch and did not dare sleep soundly.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous son was born. Mindful of the earlier tragedy, Duo charged his mother and his wife's sister to guard the child. He slept in a hut outside the door and watched through the night, never sleeping soundly.

sentences.zh: 弟能食，常自抱哺，與同臥起，十年不少怠。

translations.literal: When the younger brother could eat solid food, Duo often held him and nursed him, sleeping and rising with him; for ten years he never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Once the boy could eat, Duo often held and fed him, sleeping and waking with him, and for ten years never slackened.

sentences.zh: 弟有疾，鐸夜稽顙星斗哀禱曰：「天不伐餘家，鐸父子間可去一人，勿喪吾弟，使伯父無後也。」

translations.literal: When the younger brother fell ill, Duo at night bowed his forehead to the stars and prayed in grief, saying, "If Heaven will not destroy what remains of our house, between father and son in Duo's line one may be taken—do not let my younger brother die and leave my uncle without an heir."
translations.idiomatic: When the boy fell ill, Duo bowed to the stars at night and prayed, "If Heaven will not wipe out our house, let one of us in Duo's line be taken—but do not take my brother and leave my uncle's line without an heir."

sentences.zh: 明旦，弟愈。

translations.literal: The next morning, the younger brother recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the boy recovered.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀逾禮，廬於墓側，不理家事，宗族勸之歸，鐸曰：「今歲凶多盜，吾家雖貧，安知墓中無可欲乎！

translations.literal: When his mother died, his grief exceeded the rites; he lived in a hut beside the grave and did not attend to household affairs; clansmen urged him to return, but Duo said, "This year famine is widespread and thieves are many; though our house is poor, who knows whether the grave holds nothing worth taking!
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he grieved beyond the rites and lived in a hut beside the grave, neglecting household affairs. Kinsmen urged him home, but Duo said, "Famine and bandits are everywhere this year. Our house is poor, but who knows whether grave robbers might not disturb my mother's rest?

sentences.zh: 倘驚吾親之靈，雖生何為！」

translations.literal: If my parent's spirit were startled, what would be the use of living!"
translations.idiomatic: If I let her spirit be disturbed, what would life be worth?"

sentences.zh: 卒守廬不去。

translations.literal: In the end he kept the hut and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he kept watch at the grave and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 孫秀實，大寧人。

translations.literal: Sun Xiushi was a native of Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiushi was from Daning.

sentences.zh: 性剛毅，喜周人急​​。

translations.literal: By nature he was resolute and fond of relieving others in urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was resolute and loved to help people in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 里人王仲和嘗托秀實貸富人鈔二千錠，貧不能償，棄其親逃去。

translations.literal: A neighbor, Wang Zhonghe, once entrusted Xiushi to borrow two thousand ingots of paper money from a wealthy man; being poor, he could not repay it and abandoned his parents and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor, Wang Zhonghe, once asked Xiushi to borrow two thousand ingots from a rich man for him. Unable to repay, Zhonghe abandoned his parents and fled.

sentences.zh: 數年，其親思之，疾，秀實日饋薪米存問，終不樂。

translations.literal: After several years, his parents longed for him; they fell ill; Xiushi each day supplied firewood and grain and inquired after them, yet they were never cheered.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed. His parents pined for him and fell ill. Xiushi brought them firewood and grain every day, yet they remained inconsolable.

sentences.zh: 秀實哀之，悉為代償，取券還其親，復命奴控馬齎金，訪仲和使歸，父子歡聚，聞者莫不嗟美。

translations.literal: Xiushi mourned for them; he repaid the debt in full on their behalf, took back the bond and returned it to them, and again ordered a servant to lead a horse and carry gold to seek out Zhonghe and bring him home; father and son rejoiced in reunion, and those who heard of it all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Xiushi repaid the debt himself, returned the bond to the parents, and sent a servant with a horse and gold to find Zhonghe and bring him home. Father and son were reunited, and all who heard praised him.

sentences.zh: 又李懷玉等貸秀實鈔一千五百錠，度無以償，盡還其券不徵。

translations.literal: Also, Li Huaiyu and others had borrowed one thousand five hundred ingots from Xiushi; seeing they could not repay, they returned all the bonds and asked for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiyu and others had borrowed fifteen hundred ingots from him. Seeing they could never repay, Xiushi returned their bonds and demanded nothing.

sentences.zh: 復有賈進，大同人。

translations.literal: There was also Jia Jin, a native of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Jia Jin, from Datong.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，地震，民居多傷，且乏食，進給酒藥炭米濟之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, an earthquake struck; many dwellings were damaged and food was scarce; Jin supplied wine, medicine, charcoal, and rice to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Dade (1305), an earthquake struck. Many homes were ruined and food ran short. Jin gave out wine, medicine, charcoal, and rice.

sentences.zh: 每歲冬，制木綿裘數百襲衣寒者。

translations.literal: Every winter he made several hundred cotton-padded garments and clothed those who suffered from the cold.
translations.idiomatic: Each winter he made hundreds of cotton coats for those who shivered in the cold.

sentences.zh: 買地為義阡，使無墓者葬之。

translations.literal: He bought land as a charity burial ground so that those without graves could be buried.
translations.idiomatic: He bought land for a charity burial ground so the graveless dead could be laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 李子敬，陝西三原人。

translations.literal: Li Zijing was a native of Sanyuan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zijing was from Sanyuan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 嫁不能嫁者五十餘人，葬不能葬者五十餘喪，焚逋券四萬餘貫。

translations.literal: He provided dowries for more than fifty women who could not marry; he buried more than fifty funerals that could not be buried; he burned overdue bonds totaling more than forty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He gave dowries to more than fifty women who could not marry, buried more than fifty families who could not afford funerals, and burned overdue bonds totaling more than forty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 有司以名聞，並旌之。

translations.literal: The local officials reported their names, and all were commended.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials reported their names, and all were commended.

sentences.zh: 宗杞，大都人。

translations.literal: Zong Qi was a native of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Qi was from Dadu.

sentences.zh: 年十九，父內宰卒，擗踴號泣，絕而復蘇，水漿不入口者三日。

translations.literal: At nineteen, when his father, the palace steward, died, he beat his breast, wailed, and cried out; he stopped breathing and then revived, and for three days he took neither water nor food.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, when his father the palace steward died, he beat his breast and wailed until he collapsed. For three days he took no food or drink.

sentences.zh: 哀氣傷心，遂成疾。

translations.literal: Grief injured his heart, and he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Grief injured his heart and he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 伏臥床榻，猶哭不止，淚盡，繼之以血。

translations.literal: Prostrate on his bed, he still would not stop weeping; when his tears were exhausted, blood followed.
translations.idiomatic: Even bedridden he would not stop weeping. When his tears ran dry, he wept blood.

sentences.zh: 既葬，疾轉甚。

translations.literal: After the burial, his illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial his illness worsened.

sentences.zh: 杞有繼母，無他兄弟，度不能自起，作遺書囑其妻楊氏曰：「汝善守志，以事吾母。」

translations.literal: Qi had a stepmother and no other brothers; judging that he could not rise again, he wrote a final letter instructing his wife Lady Yang, saying, "You must keep your resolve and serve my mother."
translations.idiomatic: He had only a stepmother and no brothers. Knowing he would not recover, he wrote a final letter to his wife Lady Yang: "Keep your resolve and care for my mother."

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: He thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 楊氏遺腹生一男，人以為孝感，天不絕其嗣云。

translations.literal: Lady Yang bore a posthumous son; people took this as filial feeling moved by Heaven, saying Heaven would not cut off his line.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang bore a posthumous son. People said filial devotion had moved Heaven, and that Heaven would not end his line.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，旌其門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiding, his gate was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiding (1326), the court commended his gate.

sentences.zh: 趙榮，扶風人。

translations.literal: Zhao Rong was a native of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rong was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 母強氏有疾，榮割股肉噉之者三。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady Qiang fell ill, Rong cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to her—this he did three times.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady Qiang fell ill, Rong cut flesh from his thigh and fed it to her—three times.

sentences.zh: 复負母登太白山，禱於神，得聖水飲之，乃痊。

translations.literal: He again carried his mother on his back up Mount Taibai, prayed to the spirits, obtained sacred water for her to drink, and she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He carried his mother on his back up Mount Taibai, prayed to the spirits, and gave her sacred water to drink; she recovered.

sentences.zh: 後年七十五卒，榮號痛不食，三日方飲水，七日乃食粥。

translations.literal: Later, when she died at seventy-five, Rong wailed in grief and would not eat; only after three days did he drink water, and only after seven days did he eat gruel.
translations.idiomatic: When she died at seventy-five, Rong wailed and refused food. After three days he drank water; after seven he ate gruel.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，白雲庇其墓前後十五里，葬畢而散。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, white clouds sheltered the ground for fifteen li before and after her grave; when the burial was complete, they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day, white clouds covered fifteen li around her grave. When the rites ended, they broke apart.

sentences.zh: 榮負土成墳，廬其側終喪。

translations.literal: Rong carried earth to build the mound and lived in a hut beside it until mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Rong heaped earth for the mound and lived in a hut beside it until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 吳好直，華州蒲城人。

translations.literal: Wu Haozhi was a native of Pucheng in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Haozhi was from Pucheng in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 父歿，事繼母孝，兄弟嘗求分財，好直勸諭不能止，即以己所當得，悉推與之。

translations.literal: When his father died, he served his stepmother filially; his brothers once sought to divide the property; Haozhi admonished and exhorted them but could not stop them, so he gave them everything that would have been his share.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died, he served his stepmother filially. When his brothers wanted to split the estate, Haozhi pleaded with them in vain and gave them everything that would have been his.

sentences.zh: 出從師學，淡泊三十年，無少悔。

translations.literal: He went out to study under a teacher and lived in plain simplicity for thirty years without the slightest regret.
translations.idiomatic: He went away to study and lived plainly for thirty years without a trace of regret.

sentences.zh: 又有甄城柴鬱、陳舜諮，皆能孝友，以己產分讓兄弟。

translations.literal: There were also Chai Yu of Zhencheng and Chen Shunzi, all able in filial piety and fraternal love, who divided and yielded their property to their brothers.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Chai Yu of Zhencheng and Chen Shunzi, both filial and brotherly, who gave up their shares of the family property to their brothers.

sentences.zh: 縣令言狀，並表美之。

translations.literal: The county magistrate reported their cases, and all were marked out for praise.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate reported their cases, and all were praised.

sentences.zh: 餘丙，建德遂安人。

translations.literal: Yu Bing was a native of Suian in Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing was from Suian in Jiande.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，泣血成疾。

translations.literal: He lost his mother in childhood and wept blood until he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother as a child and wept blood until illness took him.

sentences.zh: 父亡，不忍葬，結廬古山下，殯其中，日閉戶守視。

translations.literal: When his father died, he could not bear to bury him; he built a hut beneath an old mountain, placed the coffin within, and each day closed the door and kept watch.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he could not bear burial. He built a hut beneath an old mountain, kept the coffin inside, and shut the door to guard it every day.

sentences.zh: 有牧童遺火，延殯廬，丙與子慈亟撲不止，欲投身火中，與柩俱焚。

translations.literal: A herdsboy left fire behind; the flames spread to the mourning hut; Bing and his son Ci rushed to beat them out but could not stop them; he wished to throw himself into the fire and be burned together with the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: A herdsboy's fire spread to the mourning hut. Bing and his son Ci fought the flames in vain; Bing tried to throw himself into the fire to burn with the coffin.

sentences.zh: 俄暴雨，火滅。

translations.literal: Suddenly a violent rainstorm fell, and the fire was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a torrential rain fell, and the fire went out.

sentences.zh: 徐鈺，鎮江人。

translations.literal: Xu Yu was a native of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yu was from Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 始冠，侍父鎮，將之婺源，過丹陽小溪，鎮乘橋失足，墮水中。

translations.literal: When he first came of age, he attended his father Zhen, who was going to Wuyuan; passing a small stream at Danyang, Zhen crossed a bridge, lost his footing, and fell into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Just after coming of age, he was traveling with his father Zhen to Wuyuan. At a small stream in Danyang, Zhen crossed a bridge, slipped, and fell into the water.

sentences.zh: 同行者立岸上，不能救。

translations.literal: Those traveling with him stood on the bank and could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Those with them stood on the bank, unable to reach him.

sentences.zh: 鈺投溪擁鎮出，鎮得挽行舟以升。

translations.literal: Yu leaped into the stream, embraced Zhen, and brought him out; Zhen was able to grasp a passing boat and climb aboard.
translations.idiomatic: Yu plunged into the stream, held Zhen up, and brought him out. Zhen caught a passing boat and climbed aboard.

sentences.zh: 鈺力憊，且水勢湍急，遂溺死，屍流四十五里，得於灘。

translations.literal: Yu was exhausted, and the current was swift; he drowned, and the corpse drifted forty-five li before it was found on a sandbar.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted, Yu drowned in the swift current; his body was found forty-five li downstream on a sandbar.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省言狀，表異之。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat reported the circumstances and singled him out for honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat reported the case and the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 尹莘，汴梁洧川人。

translations.literal: Yin Shen, a native of Weichuan in Bianliang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shen was from Weichuan in Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 至治初，遊學於京師，忽夢母疾，心怪之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhizhi era he went to study in the capital; suddenly he dreamed his mother was ill and thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhizhi era he studied in the capital; one night he dreamed his mother was ill and felt a foreboding.

sentences.zh: 馳歸，母已亡。

translations.literal: He rushed home; his mother had already died.
translations.idiomatic: He raced home to find his mother already dead.

sentences.zh: 居廬蔬食，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: He lived in a mourning hut, ate vegetables, and grieved until he was skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a mourning hut, ate only plain food, and wasted away in grief.

sentences.zh: 每雞鳴而起，手治祭饌，詣墓所哭奠之，風雪不廢。

translations.literal: Each day at cockcrow he rose, personally prepared sacrificial offerings, went to the grave to weep and offer them, and never stopped even in wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Each day before dawn he prepared offerings, went to the grave to mourn, and never missed a day, rain or snow.

sentences.zh: 父輔臣嘗病疫，莘侍奉湯藥，衣不解帶，嘗其糞以驗差劇，夜則禱於天曰：「莘母亡不能見，父病不能治，為人子若此，何以自立於世，願死以代父命。」

translations.literal: His father Fuchen once fell ill with plague; Shen attended with broth and medicine, never loosening his belt, tasted his stool to gauge whether the illness was improving or worsening, and at night prayed to Heaven, saying, "Shen's mother died and he could not see her; his father is ill and he cannot cure him—as a son like this, how can he stand in the world! He wishes to die in his father's place."
translations.idiomatic: When his father Fuchen had plague, Shen nursed him without rest, tasted his waste to judge the illness, and prayed at night: "My mother died before I could see her; my father is ill and I cannot save him. How can I live? Let me die in his place."

sentences.zh: 數日愈，鄉里嗟異之。

translations.literal: After several days he recovered; the village sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Fuchen recovered, and neighbors marveled.

sentences.zh: 又有高唐孫希賢，母病痢，希賢閱方書，有曰「血溫身熱者死，血冷身涼者生」。

translations.literal: There was also Sun Xixian of Gaotang—his mother had dysentery; Xixian read medical books and found a passage saying, "If the blood is warm and the body hot, death; if the blood is cold and the body cool, life."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xixian of Gaotang—when his mother had dysentery he read medical texts: "Warm blood and a hot body mean death; cold blood and a cool body mean life."

sentences.zh: 希賢嘗之，其血溫，乃號泣祈天，求身代之，母遂愈。

translations.literal: Xixian tasted it; the blood was warm; he then wailed and prayed to Heaven, asking to take her place, and his mother recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He tasted her blood—it was warm. He wailed and prayed to take her place, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 高郵卜勝榮，母痢，不能藥，日嘗痢以求愈。

translations.literal: Bu Shengrong of Gaoyou—his mother had dysentery and medicine did not help; each day he tasted the dysentery, seeking her recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Shengrong of Gaoyou—when his mother had dysentery uncured by medicine, he tasted it daily, hoping she would heal.

sentences.zh: 兄疾，禮北辰，乞減己年延之。

translations.literal: When his elder brother fell ill, he performed rites to the North Star, begging to shorten his own years to extend his brother's.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother fell ill, he prayed to the North Star to shorten his own life and add to his brother's.

sentences.zh: 並痊。

translations.literal: All recovered.
translations.idiomatic: All of them recovered.

sentences.zh: 劉廷讓，大寧武平人。

translations.literal: Liu Tingrang, a native of Wuping in Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tingrang was from Wuping in Daning.

sentences.zh: 至順初，北方兵起，民被殺掠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhishun era, when northern troops rose, the people were killed and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhishun era, when northern armies rose, people were killed and robbed.

sentences.zh: 廷讓挈家避山中，有幼弟方乳，母王氏置於懷，兵急，廷讓乃棄己子，一手抱幼弟，一手扶母，疾驅得免。

translations.literal: Tingrang led his family to flee into the mountains; he had a younger brother still nursing; his mother Lady Wang carried him in her arms; when troops pressed close, Tingrang abandoned his own child, took the infant brother in one arm and supported his mother with the other, and galloped away to safety.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing to the mountains with his family, he had a nursing brother. As soldiers closed in, he abandoned his own child, carried the baby in one arm, supported his mother with the other, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 事聞，旌之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court conferred commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Once officials heard of it, the court honored him.

sentences.zh: 劉通，亳州譙縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Tong, a native of Qiao County in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tong was from Qiao County in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧業農。

translations.literal: The family was poor and farmed for a living.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor and lived by farming.

sentences.zh: 母卜氏，好聲樂，每眩技者以簫鼓至門，必令娛侍，或自歌舞，以悅母心。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Bu loved music; whenever performers with flute and drum came to the door, she always had them entertain and wait on her, or she herself sang and danced to please her mother's heart.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Bu loved music. When musicians came to the door, he had them perform for her, or sang and danced himself to please her.

sentences.zh: 卜氏目失明，通誓斷酒肉，禱之三十年不懈。

translations.literal: Lady Bu's eyes went blind; Tong vowed to abstain from wine and meat and prayed for thirty years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When she went blind, Tong swore off wine and meat and prayed for thirty years without fail.

sentences.zh: 卜氏年八十五，忽復明。

translations.literal: Lady Bu was eighty-five when her sight suddenly returned.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty-five her sight suddenly returned.

sentences.zh: 至大間鄱陽黃鎰，皇慶間諸暨丁祥一，皆以親喪明，以舌舐之，復能視。

translations.literal: During the Zhida era Huang Yi of Poyang, and during the Huangqing era Ding Xiangyi of Zhuji—both when their parents' eyes failed, licked them with the tongue and sight returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yi of Poyang in the Zhida era and Ding Xiangyi of Zhuji in the Huangqing era—when parents went blind, licked their eyes and sight returned.

sentences.zh: 並命褒表。

translations.literal: All were ordered commended with honorific placards.
translations.idiomatic: All were ordered commended with inscribed placards.

sentences.zh: 張旺舅，安豐霍丘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wangjiu, a native of Huoqiu in Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wangjiu was from Huoqiu in Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 幼失父，母陳氏居貧守志。

translations.literal: He lost his father young; his mother Lady Chen lived in poverty and kept her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: His father died young; his mother Lady Chen lived in poverty and kept her widowhood.

sentences.zh: 旺舅九歲，賣錫以養。

translations.literal: At nine Wangjiu sold tin to support her.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he sold tin to support her.

sentences.zh: 及長，母病，伏枕數月，旺舅無貲命醫，惟日夜痛哭，禮天求代，未幾遂愈。

translations.literal: When he grew up his mother fell ill and lay on her pillow for months; Wangjiu had no money to hire a physician and only wept day and night, praying to Heaven to take her place; before long she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill for months he had no money for doctors; he wept and prayed to die in her place, and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 又自以生業微不能多給，竟不娶，以終母年。

translations.literal: He also considered his livelihood too small to provide abundantly and in the end did not marry, serving her until her years ended.
translations.idiomatic: His earnings were modest; he never married and cared for her until she died.

sentences.zh: 縣令言於朝，旌之。

translations.literal: The county magistrate reported to the court, and he was honored.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate reported his case and he was commended.

sentences.zh: 張思孝，華州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Sixiao, a native of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sixiao was from Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 母喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 父疾，調護甚至，不愈，以父涕洟半器，垂泣盡飲之，复潔齋致禱，乞以身代，未幾，遂痊。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill he tended him with utmost care; when he did not recover, he took half a vessel of his father's nasal discharge, wept as he drank it all, then purified himself and prayed, begging to take his father's place; before long he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell gravely ill, Sixiao nursed him tirelessly. When medicine failed, he drank half a bowl of his father's phlegm, wept, purified himself, and prayed to die in his place—and his father recovered.

sentences.zh: 至順三年，表其門。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhishun, an honorific placard was displayed at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhishun (1332) his gate was honored with a placard.

sentences.zh: 杜佑，邳州人。

translations.literal: Du You, a native of Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was from Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 河南行省署為三叉口水、馬站提領。

translations.literal: The Henan Branch Secretariat appointed him clerk of the Sanchakou water and horse station.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Branch Secretariat appointed him clerk at the Sanchakou water and horse station.

sentences.zh: 父成病於家，佑忽心驚，舉體沾汗，即棄職歸。

translations.literal: His father Cheng fell ill at home; You suddenly felt his heart startled, sweat poured over his body, and he immediately resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Cheng fell ill at home, You felt a sudden dread, broke out in sweat, and resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 父病始三日，遂禱神求代，且嘗糞以驗疾。

translations.literal: His father's illness had just begun three days before; he prayed to the spirits to take his place and tasted the stool to gauge the illness.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days of the illness he prayed to take his father's place and tasted his waste to judge its severity.

sentences.zh: 父卒，廬墓盡哀，有馴兔之瑞。

translations.literal: When his father died he built a mourning hut and grieved to the full extent; tame hares appeared as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died he kept a mourning hut with full grief; tame hares appeared as a blessing.

sentences.zh: 長壽，父帖住，官平章政事，生五子。

translations.literal: Changshou—his father Tiezhu served as Grand Councilor and had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou's father Tiezhu was Grand Councilor and had five sons.

sentences.zh: 長山壽早世，次即長壽，次永壽、福壽、忙古海牙。

translations.literal: The eldest Shanshou died young; next was Changshou, then Yongshou, Fushou, and Manguhaiya.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Shanshou died young; then Changshou, Yongshou, Fushou, and Manguhaiya.

sentences.zh: 元統間，帖住歿，長壽哀毀盡禮。

translations.literal: During the Yuantong era Tiezhu died; Changshou mourned with full propriety.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuantong Tiezhu died; Changshou mourned with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 服闋，當廕敘，與弟羅拜母前曰：「吾父廉貧，諸弟未有所立，願以職讓永壽。」

translations.literal: When mourning ended and he was due for hereditary appointment, he and his brothers bowed before their mother and said, "Our father was honest and poor; our younger brothers have not yet established themselves—we wish to yield the office to Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended and hereditary office came due, he and his brothers bowed to their mother: "Father was poor and honest; our younger brothers are unsettled. We yield the appointment to Yongshou."

sentences.zh: 永壽讓福壽，福壽曰：「二兄能讓，福壽獨不能耶！」

translations.literal: Yongshou yielded to Fushou; Fushou said, "Both elder brothers can yield—can Fushou alone not do so!
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou yielded to Fushou. Fushou said, "If both elder brothers can yield, why can't I?"

sentences.zh: 以讓忙古海牙，母從之。

translations.literal: They yielded to Manguhaiya, and their mother consented.
translations.idiomatic: They yielded to Manguhaiya, and their mother agreed.

sentences.zh: 忙古海牙遂告廕，為太禧宗禋院神御殿侍禮佐郎，階奉議大夫。

translations.literal: Manguhaiya then reported for hereditary appointment as assistant ritual attendant of the Spirit Hall in the Grand Sacrifices Administration, rank Submitted Discussion Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Manguhaiya took the hereditary post as assistant ritual attendant in the Grand Sacrifices Administration, rank Submitted Discussion Grandee.

sentences.zh: 兄弟奉母尤篤，邦閭美之。

translations.literal: The brothers served their mother with especial devotion; the district praised them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers cared for their mother with deep devotion; neighbors praised them.

sentences.zh: 至大間，河中梁外僧，親喪廬墓，兄那海為奧魯官，自以嘗遠仕，不得養其親，即棄職，舉外僧代之。

translations.literal: During the Zhida era Liang Waiseng of Hezhong, when his parents died, lived in a mourning hut at the grave; his elder brother Naihai served as aurug official and, thinking he had long been far in office and could not nourish his parents, immediately resigned and had Waiseng replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhida era, Hezhong's Liang Waiseng mourned at his parents' grave. Elder brother Naihai, an aurug officer, resigned because he had served far from home and could not care for them, letting Waiseng take his place.

sentences.zh: 人稱外僧能孝，那海能義。

translations.literal: People called Waiseng filial and Naihai righteous.
translations.idiomatic: People praised Waiseng for filial piety and Naihai for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 又有畏吾氏秋秋，及濠州高中、嘉定武進，皆以侍親不願仕，以祖父廕讓叔父昆弟云。

translations.literal: There were also Qiqiu of the Uyghurs, and Gao Zhong of Haozhou and Wu Jin of Jiading—all unwilling to take office while serving parents, yielding hereditary appointments to uncles and brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Also the Uyghur Qiqiu, Haozhou's Gao Zhong, and Jiading's Wu Jin—all declined office to serve parents and yielded hereditary posts to kin.

sentences.zh: 孫瑾，鎮江丹徒人。

translations.literal: Sun Jin, a native of Dantu in Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jin was from Dantu in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 父喪，哀毀，嚴冬跣足而步，停柩四載，衣不解帶，常食粥，誦佛書。

translations.literal: When his father died he grieved in mourning; in severe winter he walked barefoot; the coffin rested four years; he never loosened his belt, always ate gruel, and chanted Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he mourned barefoot even in harsh winter. The coffin rested four years; he never loosened his belt, ate only gruel, and chanted sutras.

sentences.zh: 及葬，載柩渡江，潮波方湧，俄順風翼帆，如履平地。

translations.literal: At burial, as the coffin was ferried across the river, the tide was surging; suddenly a favorable wind filled the sails and it was as if walking on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin crossed the river at burial, the tide was fierce; suddenly a fair wind filled the sails and the crossing was smooth as dry land.

sentences.zh: 事繼母唐氏尤孝，嘗患癰，瑾親吮之；

translations.literal: He served his stepmother Lady Tang with especial filial piety; she once had a carbuncle and Jin personally sucked it;
translations.idiomatic: He served stepmother Lady Tang with deep devotion; when she had a boil he sucked it clean;

sentences.zh: 又喪目，瑾舐之復明。

translations.literal: when she lost her sight, Jin licked her eyes and sight returned.
translations.idiomatic: when she went blind he licked her eyes and she could see again.

sentences.zh: 唐氏卒，卜日將葬，時春苦雨，瑾夜號天乞霽，至旦，雲日開朗。

translations.literal: When Lady Tang died and a burial day was chosen, spring brought bitter rain; Jin cried to Heaven at night begging for clear weather, and by dawn clouds parted and the sun shone.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Tang died, endless spring rain threatened the burial. Jin prayed all night for clear skies; by dawn the sun broke through.

sentences.zh: 甫掩壙，陰氣復合，雨注數日不止。

translations.literal: Just as the grave was covered, yin clouds joined again and rain poured for days without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The moment the grave was sealed, clouds closed again and rain fell for days.

sentences.zh: 又有吳希曾，睢寧人。

translations.literal: There was also Wu Xizeng of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wu Xizeng of Suining.

sentences.zh: 父卒，葬之日大雨，希曾跪柩前，炷艾燃腕，火熾，雨止。

translations.literal: On the day his father was buried it rained heavily; Xizeng knelt before the coffin, burned moxa on his wrist until the fire blazed, and the rain stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's burial day, as rain poured, Xizeng knelt before the coffin and burned moxa on his wrist until the rain ceased.

sentences.zh: 既葬，廬於墓左。

translations.literal: After burial he built a hut to the left of the grave.
translations.idiomatic: After burial he kept a hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 縣上狀，並旌之。

translations.literal: The county submitted a report, and all were honored.
translations.idiomatic: The county reported their cases and all were commended.

sentences.zh: 張恭，河南偃師人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gong, a native of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gong was from Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 以兵部符署鷹房府案牘，親老，辭歸侍養，墾理先墓，身負水灌松柏。

translations.literal: By military ministry order he served as clerk in the Eagle House office; his parents were old and he resigned to return home and serve them, reclaimed the ancestral graves, and personally carried water to irrigate the pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as clerk in the Eagle House, he resigned when his parents aged, tended the ancestral graves, and carried water himself for the pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 父喪，過哀。

translations.literal: When his father died his grief exceeded measure.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died his grief was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 侍母馮氏尤謹。

translations.literal: He served his mother Lady Feng all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his mother Lady Feng with even greater devotion.

sentences.zh: 歲凶，恭夫婦採野菜為食，而營奉甘旨無乏。

translations.literal: In a famine year Gong and his wife gathered wild vegetables for food yet never lacked fine provisions for her.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he and his wife ate wild greens yet never let her want for good food.

sentences.zh: 母有疾，恭手除溷穢，餵哺飲食，且嘗糞以驗疾勢。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Gong personally removed her waste, fed and nursed her, and tasted her stool to gauge the illness.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill he cleaned her waste, fed her by hand, and tasted her stool to judge the illness.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，西兵至河南，居民悉竄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianli era, when western troops reached Henan, all residents fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianli era, when western troops entered Henan, everyone fled.

sentences.zh: 恭守視母病，項中一劍，不去。

translations.literal: Gong stayed to watch over his ill mother; a sword at his neck, he would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Gong stayed with his sick mother—a sword at his neck could not make him leave.

sentences.zh: 母驚悸而歿，恭居喪盡禮，人稱孝焉。

translations.literal: His mother died of fright; Gong observed mourning with full propriety, and people called him filial.
translations.idiomatic: She died of fright; Gong mourned with full rites and neighbors called him filial.

sentences.zh: 有詔旌其閭。

translations.literal: An edict honored his gate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his household.

sentences.zh: 訾汝道，德州齊河人。

translations.literal: Zi Rudao, a native of Qihe in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Rudao was from Qihe in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 父興卒，居喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his father Xing died he observed mourning and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Xing died he mourned and was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 母高氏治家嚴，汝道承順甚恭。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Gao ran the household strictly; Rudao complied and served with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Gao ran a strict household; Rudao obeyed her with humble respect.

sentences.zh: 母嘗寢疾，晝夜不去側。

translations.literal: When his mother once lay ill he day and night would not leave her side.
translations.idiomatic: When she lay ill he never left her side day or night.

sentences.zh: 一日，母屏人授以金珠若干曰：「汝素孝，室無私蓄，我一旦不諱，此物非汝有矣，可善藏之，毋令他兄弟知也。」

translations.literal: One day his mother dismissed others and gave him a quantity of gold and pearls, saying, "You have always been filial and keep no private store; if I should die unexpectedly, these things would no longer be yours—you should hide them well and let no other brother know.
translations.idiomatic: One day she sent others away and gave him gold and pearls: "You are filial and keep nothing for yourself. If I die suddenly, hide these—do not let your brothers know."

sentences.zh: 汝道泣拜曰：「吾父母起艱難，成家業，今田宅牛羊已多，汝道恨無以報大恩，尚敢受此，以重不孝之罪乎！」

translations.literal: Rudao wept and bowed, saying, "My parents rose from hardship and built the household; now fields, dwellings, cattle, and sheep are many—Rudao regrets he has no way to repay the great grace; how dare he accept this and add to the crime of unfiliality!"
translations.idiomatic: Rudao wept and refused: "Our parents built this estate from hardship. I have no way to repay you—how could I take this and deepen my unfiliality?"

sentences.zh: 竟辭之。

translations.literal: In the end he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He would not accept.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀，終喪不御酒肉。

translations.literal: When his mother died his grief was devastating; through the whole mourning period he touched neither wine nor meat.
translations.idiomatic: When she died he grieved utterly and took no wine or meat for the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 性尤友愛，二弟將析居，汝道悉以美田廬讓之；

translations.literal: By nature he was especially brotherly; when his two younger brothers were about to divide the household, Rudao yielded to them all the fine fields and houses;
translations.idiomatic: Deeply brotherly, when his two younger brothers split the household he gave them all the best land and houses;

sentences.zh: 二弟早世，撫諸孤如己子。

translations.literal: when the two brothers died young he raised their orphans as his own.
translations.idiomatic: when both died young he raised their children as his own.

sentences.zh: 鄉人劉顯等貧無以為生，汝道割己田各畀之，使食其租終身。

translations.literal: Neighbors Liu Xian and others were too poor to live; Rudao divided his own fields and gave each a share, letting them eat the rent for life.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors like Liu Xian were destitute; Rudao gave each a parcel of his own land to live on for life.

sentences.zh: 里中嘗大疫，有食瓜得汗而癒者，汝道即多市瓜及攜米，歷戶饋之。

translations.literal: When a great plague struck the village, some recovered by eating melons and sweating; Rudao bought many melons and carried rice, going door to door to give them.
translations.idiomatic: When plague struck, some recovered after eating melons and sweating; Rudao bought melons and rice and brought them to every door.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「癘氣能染人，勿入也。」

translations.literal: Some said, "The pestilence can infect people—do not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Some warned, "The sickness spreads—stay out."

sentences.zh: 不聽，益周行問所苦，然卒無恙。

translations.literal: He would not listen and went all the more widely to ask what ailed them, yet in the end suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored them, went from house to house asking after the sick, and never fell ill.

sentences.zh: 有死者，复贈以槥櫝，人咸感之。

translations.literal: For those who died he again gave coffins; all were moved.
translations.idiomatic: For the dead he gave coffins; all were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 嘗出麥粟貸人，至秋，蝗食稼，人無以償，汝道聚其券焚之。

translations.literal: He once lent out wheat and grain; when autumn came locusts ate the crops and people could not repay; Rudao gathered the bonds and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He had lent grain; when locusts ruined the harvest and debtors could not pay, he burned their IOUs.

sentences.zh: 縣令李讓為請旌其家。

translations.literal: Magistrate Li Rang petitioned to honor his household.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Rang petitioned to commend his household.
